cura.build_volume_fan_nr.label: Build volume fan number
cura.build_volume_fan_nr.tooltip: The number of the fan that cools the build volume. If this is set to 0, it's means that there is no build volume fan

cura.machine_name.label: Machine Type
cura.machine_name.tooltip: The name of your 3D printer model.

cura.machine_show_variants.label: Show Machine Variants
cura.machine_show_variants.tooltip: Whether to show the different variants of this machine, which are described in separate json files.

cura.material_guid.label: Material GUID
cura.material_guid.tooltip: The unique ID of the material.

cura.material_bed_temp_wait.label: Wait for Build Plate Heatup
cura.material_bed_temp_wait.tooltip: Whether to insert a command to wait until the build plate temperature is reached at the start.

cura.material_print_temp_wait.label: Wait for Nozzle Heatup
cura.material_print_temp_wait.tooltip: Whether to wait until the nozzle temperature is reached at the start.

cura.material_print_temp_prepend.label: Include Material Temperatures
cura.material_print_temp_prepend.tooltip: Whether to include nozzle temperature commands at the start of the gcode. When the start_gcode already contains nozzle temperature commands Cura frontend will automatically disable this setting.

cura.material_bed_temp_prepend.label: Include Build Plate Temperature
cura.material_bed_temp_prepend.tooltip: Whether to include build plate temperature commands at the start of the gcode. When the start_gcode already contains build plate temperature commands Cura frontend will automatically disable this setting.

cura.machine_shape.label: Build Plate Shape
cura.machine_shape.tooltip: The shape of the build plate without taking unprintable areas into account.

cura.machine_buildplate_type.label: Build Plate Type
cura.machine_buildplate_type.tooltip: The type of build plate installed on the printer.

cura.machine_heated_bed.label: Has Heated Build Plate
cura.machine_heated_bed.tooltip: Whether the machine has a heated build plate present.

cura.machine_heated_build_volume.label: Has Build Volume Temperature Stabilization
cura.machine_heated_build_volume.tooltip: Whether the machine is able to stabilize the build volume temperature.

cura.machine_always_write_active_tool.label: Always Write Active Tool
cura.machine_always_write_active_tool.tooltip: Write active tool after sending temp commands to inactive tool. Required for Dual Extruder printing with Smoothie or other firmware with modal tool commands.

cura.machine_center_is_zero.label: Is Center Origin
cura.machine_center_is_zero.tooltip: Whether the X/Y coordinates of the zero position of the printer is at the center of the printable area.

cura.machine_extruder_count.label: Number of Extruders
cura.machine_extruder_count.tooltip: Number of extruder trains. An extruder train is the combination of a feeder, bowden tube, and nozzle.

cura.extruders_enabled_count.label: Number of Extruders That Are Enabled
cura.extruders_enabled_count.tooltip: Number of extruder trains that are enabled; automatically set in software

cura.machine_nozzle_tip_outer_diameter.label: Outer Nozzle Diameter
cura.machine_nozzle_tip_outer_diameter.tooltip: The outer diameter of the tip of the nozzle.

cura.machine_nozzle_expansion_angle.label: Nozzle Angle
cura.machine_nozzle_expansion_angle.tooltip: The angle between the horizontal plane and the conical part right above the tip of the nozzle.

cura.machine_heat_zone_length.label: Heat Zone Length
cura.machine_heat_zone_length.tooltip: The distance from the tip of the nozzle in which heat from the nozzle is transferred to the filament.

cura.machine_nozzle_temp_enabled.label: Enable Nozzle Temperature Control
cura.machine_nozzle_temp_enabled.tooltip: Whether to control temperature from Cura. Turn this off to control nozzle temperature from outside of Cura.

cura.machine_nozzle_heat_up_speed.label: Heat Up Speed
cura.machine_nozzle_heat_up_speed.tooltip: The speed (°C/s) by which the nozzle heats up averaged over the window of normal printing temperatures and the standby temperature.

cura.machine_nozzle_cool_down_speed.label: Cool Down Speed
cura.machine_nozzle_cool_down_speed.tooltip: The speed (°C/s) by which the nozzle cools down averaged over the window of normal printing temperatures and the standby temperature.

cura.machine_min_cool_heat_time_window.label: Minimal Time Standby Temperature
cura.machine_min_cool_heat_time_window.tooltip: The minimal time an extruder has to be inactive before the nozzle is cooled. Only when an extruder is not used for longer than this time will it be allowed to cool down to the standby temperature.

cura.machine_extruders_share_heater.label: Extruders Share Heater
cura.machine_extruders_share_heater.tooltip: Whether the extruders share a single heater rather than each extruder having its own heater.

cura.machine_extruders_share_nozzle.label: Extruders Share Nozzle
cura.machine_extruders_share_nozzle.tooltip: Whether the extruders share a single nozzle rather than each extruder having its own nozzle. When set to true, it is expected that the printer-start gcode script properly sets up all extruders in an initial retraction state that is known and mutually compatible (either zero or one filament not retracted); in that case the initial retraction status is described, per extruder, by the 'machine_extruders_shared_nozzle_initial_retraction' parameter.

cura.machine_extruders_shared_nozzle_ini.label: Shared Nozzle Initial Retraction
cura.machine_extruders_shared_nozzle_ini.tooltip: How much the filament of each extruder is assumed to have been retracted from the shared nozzle tip at the completion of the printer-start gcode script; the value should be equal to or greater than the length of the common part of the nozzle's ducts.

cura.machine_disallowed_areas.label: Disallowed Areas
cura.machine_disallowed_areas.tooltip: A list of polygons with areas the print head is not allowed to enter.

cura.nozzle_disallowed_areas.label: Nozzle Disallowed Areas
cura.nozzle_disallowed_areas.tooltip: A list of polygons with areas the nozzle is not allowed to enter.

cura.machine_head_with_fans_polygon.label: Machine Head & Fan Polygon
cura.machine_head_with_fans_polygon.tooltip: The dimensions of the print head used to determine 'Safe Model Distance' when printing 'One at a Time'. These numbers relate to the centerline of the first extruder nozzle. Left of the nozzle is 'X Min' and must be negative.  Rear of the nozzle is 'Y Min' and must be negative.  X Max (right) and Y Max (front) are positive numbers.  Gantry height is the dimension from the build plate to the X gantry beam.

cura.machine_time_estimation_factor.label: Print Time Estimation Factor
cura.machine_time_estimation_factor.tooltip: Multiplier for adjusting print time estimates. 100% shows original estimate. Higher values indicate longer actual print times.

cura.machine_nozzle_id.label: Nozzle ID
cura.machine_nozzle_id.tooltip: The nozzle ID for an extruder train, such as "AA 0.4" and "BB 0.8".

cura.machine_use_extruder_offset_to_offs.label: Offset with Extruder
cura.machine_use_extruder_offset_to_offs.tooltip: Apply the extruder offset to the coordinate system. Affects all extruders.

cura.machine_start_gcode_first.label: Start GCode must be first
cura.machine_start_gcode_first.tooltip: This setting controls if the start-gcode is forced to always be the first g-code. Without this option other g-code, such as a T0 can be inserted before the start g-code.

cura.extruder_prime_pos_z.label: Extruder Prime Z Position
cura.extruder_prime_pos_z.tooltip: The Z coordinate of the position where the nozzle primes at the start of printing.

cura.extruder_prime_pos_abs.label: Absolute Extruder Prime Position
cura.extruder_prime_pos_abs.tooltip: Make the extruder prime position absolute rather than relative to the last-known location of the head.

cura.machine_acceleration.label: Default Acceleration
cura.machine_acceleration.tooltip: The default acceleration of print head movement.

cura.machine_max_jerk_xy.label: Default X-Y Jerk
cura.machine_max_jerk_xy.tooltip: Default jerk for movement in the horizontal plane.

cura.machine_steps_per_mm_x.label: Steps per Millimeter (X)
cura.machine_steps_per_mm_x.tooltip: How many steps of the stepper motor will result in one millimeter of movement in the X direction.

cura.machine_steps_per_mm_y.label: Steps per Millimeter (Y)
cura.machine_steps_per_mm_y.tooltip: How many steps of the stepper motor will result in one millimeter of movement in the Y direction.

cura.machine_steps_per_mm_z.label: Steps per Millimeter (Z)
cura.machine_steps_per_mm_z.tooltip: How many steps of the stepper motor will result in one millimeter of movement in the Z direction.

cura.machine_steps_per_mm_e.label: Steps per Millimeter (E)
cura.machine_steps_per_mm_e.tooltip: How many steps of the stepper motors will result in moving the feeder wheel by one millimeter around its circumference.

cura.machine_endstop_positive_direction_.label: X Endstop in Positive Direction
cura.machine_endstop_positive_direction_.tooltip: Whether the endstop of the X axis is in the positive direction (high X coordinate) or negative (low X coordinate).

cura.machine_endstop_positive_direction_.label: Y Endstop in Positive Direction
cura.machine_endstop_positive_direction_.tooltip: Whether the endstop of the Y axis is in the positive direction (high Y coordinate) or negative (low Y coordinate).

cura.machine_endstop_positive_direction_.label: Z Endstop in Positive Direction
cura.machine_endstop_positive_direction_.tooltip: Whether the endstop of the Z axis is in the positive direction (high Z coordinate) or negative (low Z coordinate).

cura.machine_minimum_feedrate.label: Minimum Feedrate
cura.machine_minimum_feedrate.tooltip: The minimal movement speed of the print head.

cura.machine_feeder_wheel_diameter.label: Feeder Wheel Diameter
cura.machine_feeder_wheel_diameter.tooltip: The diameter of the wheel that drives the material in the feeder.

cura.machine_scale_fan_speed_zero_to_one.label: Scale Fan Speed To 0-1
cura.machine_scale_fan_speed_zero_to_one.tooltip: Scale the fan speed to be between 0 and 1 instead of between 0 and 256.

cura.reset_flow_duration.label: Reset flow duration
cura.reset_flow_duration.tooltip: For any travel move longer than this value, the material flow is reset to the paths target flow

cura.wall_line_width.label: Wall Line Width
cura.wall_line_width.tooltip: Width of a single wall line.

cura.skin_line_width.label: Top/Bottom Line Width
cura.skin_line_width.tooltip: Width of a single top/bottom line.

cura.skirt_brim_line_width.label: Skirt/Brim Line Width
cura.skirt_brim_line_width.tooltip: Width of a single skirt or brim line.

cura.support_interface_line_width.label: Support Interface Line Width
cura.support_interface_line_width.tooltip: Width of a single line of support roof or floor.

cura.support_roof_line_width.label: Support Roof Line Width
cura.support_roof_line_width.tooltip: Width of a single support roof line.

cura.support_bottom_line_width.label: Support Floor Line Width
cura.support_bottom_line_width.tooltip: Width of a single support floor line.

cura.prime_tower_line_width.label: Prime Tower Line Width
cura.prime_tower_line_width.tooltip: Width of a single prime tower line.

cura.initial_layer_line_width_factor.label: Initial Layer Line Width
cura.initial_layer_line_width_factor.tooltip: Multiplier of the line width on the first layer. Increasing this could improve bed adhesion.

cura.wall_extruder_nr.label: Wall Extruder
cura.wall_extruder_nr.tooltip: The extruder train used for printing the walls. This is used in multi-extrusion.

cura.wall_0_extruder_nr.label: Outer Wall Extruder
cura.wall_0_extruder_nr.tooltip: The extruder train used for printing the outer wall. This is used in multi-extrusion.

cura.wall_x_extruder_nr.label: Inner Wall Extruder
cura.wall_x_extruder_nr.tooltip: The extruder train used for printing the inner walls. This is used in multi-extrusion.

cura.wall_thickness.label: Wall Thickness
cura.wall_thickness.tooltip: The thickness of the walls in the horizontal direction. This value divided by the wall line width defines the number of walls.

cura.wall_transition_filter_distance.label: Wall Transitioning Filter Distance
cura.wall_transition_filter_distance.tooltip: If it would be transitioning back and forth between different numbers of walls in quick succession, don't transition at all. Remove transitions if they are closer together than this distance.

cura.wall_0_wipe_dist.label: Outer Wall Wipe Distance
cura.wall_0_wipe_dist.tooltip: Distance of a travel move inserted after the outer wall, to hide the Z seam better.

default.expr: (machine_nozzle_size - wall_line_width_0) / 2 if (wall_line_width_0 < machine_nozzle_size and inset_direction != "outside_in") else 0

cura.wall_0_inset.label: Outer Wall Inset
cura.wall_0_inset.tooltip: Inset applied to the path of the outer wall. If the outer wall is smaller than the nozzle, and printed after the inner walls, use this offset to get the hole in the nozzle to overlap with the inner walls instead of the outside of the model.

cura.wall_x_inset.label: Inner Wall Inset
cura.wall_x_inset.tooltip: Inset applied to the path of the inner wall(s). The infill will move along with the new boundary set by the innermost inner wall

cura.optimize_wall_printing_order.label: Optimize Wall Printing Order
cura.optimize_wall_printing_order.tooltip: Optimize the order in which walls are printed so as to reduce the number of retractions and the distance travelled. Most parts will benefit from this being enabled but some may actually take longer so please compare the print time estimates with and without optimization. First layer is not optimized when choosing brim as build plate adhesion type.

cura.inset_direction.label: Wall Ordering
cura.inset_direction.tooltip: Determines the order in which walls are printed. Printing outer walls earlier helps with dimensional accuracy, as faults from inner walls cannot propagate to the outside. However printing them later allows them to stack better when overhangs are printed. When there is an uneven amount of total innner walls, the 'center last line' is always printed last.

cura.initial_layer_inset_direction.label: Initial Layer Wall Ordering
cura.initial_layer_inset_direction.tooltip: Determines the order in which walls are printed on the initial layer. This allows different wall ordering specifically for the first layer to improve bed adhesion. When not changed by user, the Wall Ordering setting value is used.

cura.alternate_extra_perimeter.label: Alternate Extra Wall
cura.alternate_extra_perimeter.tooltip: Prints an extra wall at every other layer. This way infill gets caught between these extra walls, resulting in stronger prints.

cura.min_wall_line_width.label: Minimum Wall Line Width
cura.min_wall_line_width.tooltip: For thin structures around once or twice the nozzle size, the line widths need to be altered to adhere to the thickness of the model. This setting controls the minimum line width allowed for the walls. The minimum line widths inherently also determine the maximum line widths, since we transition from N to N+1 walls at some geometry thickness where the N walls are wide and the N+1 walls are narrow. The widest possible wall line is twice the Minimum Wall Line Width.

cura.min_even_wall_line_width.label: Minimum Even Wall Line Width
cura.min_even_wall_line_width.tooltip: The minimum line width for normal polygonal walls. This setting determines at which model thickness we switch from printing a single thin wall line, to printing two wall lines. A higher Minimum Even Wall Line Width leads to a higher maximum odd wall line width. The maximum even wall line width is calculated as Outer Wall Line Width + 0.5 * Minimum Odd Wall Line Width.

cura.min_odd_wall_line_width.label: Minimum Odd Wall Line Width
cura.min_odd_wall_line_width.tooltip: The minimum line width for middle line gap filler polyline walls. This setting determines at which model thickness we switch from printing two wall lines, to printing two outer walls and a single central wall in the middle. A higher Minimum Odd Wall Line Width leads to a higher maximum even wall line width. The maximum odd wall line width is calculated as 2 * Minimum Even Wall Line Width.

cura.fill_outline_gaps.label: Print Thin Walls
cura.fill_outline_gaps.tooltip: Print pieces of the model which are horizontally thinner than the nozzle size.

cura.hole_xy_offset_max_diameter.label: Hole Horizontal Expansion Max Diameter
cura.hole_xy_offset_max_diameter.tooltip: When greater than zero, the Hole Horizontal Expansion is gradually applied on small holes (small holes are expanded more). When set to zero the Hole Horizontal Expansion will be applied to all holes. Holes larger than the Hole Horizontal Expansion Max Diameter are not expanded.

cura.z_seam_on_vertex.label: Z Seam On Vertex
cura.z_seam_on_vertex.tooltip: Place the z-seam on a polygon vertex. Switching this off can place the seam between vertices as well. (Keep in mind that this won't override the restrictions on placing the seam on an unsupported overhang.)

cura.z_seam_position.label: Z Seam Position
cura.z_seam_position.tooltip: The position near where to start printing each part in a layer. Note: For the 'Middle' option, the reference point differs critically based on Z Seam Relative setting - it will be the middle of the buildplate (absolute) or the middle of each object (relative), resulting in completely different seam placements.

default.expr: (0 if (z_seam_position == 'frontleft' or z_seam_position == 'left' or z_seam_position == 'backleft') else machine_width / 2 if (z_seam_position == 'front' or z_seam_position == 'back' or z_seam_position == 'middle') else machine_width) - (machine_width / 2 if z_seam_relative or machine_center_is_zero else 0)

cura.z_seam_x.label: Z Seam X
cura.z_seam_x.tooltip: The X coordinate of the position near where to start printing each part in a layer. When Z Seam Relative is disabled, this is an absolute position on the buildplate. When enabled, this is relative to each object's center.

default.expr: (0 if (z_seam_position == 'frontleft' or z_seam_position == 'front' or z_seam_position == 'frontright') else machine_depth / 2 if (z_seam_position == 'left' or z_seam_position == 'right' or z_seam_position == 'middle') else machine_depth) - (machine_depth / 2 if z_seam_relative or machine_center_is_zero else 0)

cura.z_seam_y.label: Z Seam Y
cura.z_seam_y.tooltip: The Y coordinate of the position near where to start printing each part in a layer. When Z Seam Relative is disabled, this is an absolute position on the buildplate. When enabled, this is relative to each object's center.

cura.z_seam_corner.label: Seam Corner Preference
cura.z_seam_corner.tooltip: Control how corners on the model outline influence the position of the seam. Hide Seam makes the seam more likely to occur on an inside corner. Expose Seam makes the seam more likely to occur on an outside corner. Hide or Expose Seam makes the seam more likely to occur at an inside or outside corner. Smart Hiding allows both inside and outside corners, but chooses inside corners more frequently, if appropriate.

cura.z_seam_relative.label: Z Seam Relative
cura.z_seam_relative.tooltip: When enabled, the z seam coordinates are relative to each part's centre. When disabled, the coordinates define an absolute position on the build plate. This setting is critical for the 'Middle' Z Seam Position option: relative positioning places the seam at the middle of each object, while absolute positioning places it at the middle of the buildplate, resulting in completely different seam placements.

cura.roofing_extruder_nr.label: Top Surface Skin Extruder
cura.roofing_extruder_nr.tooltip: The extruder train used for printing the top most skin. This is used in multi-extrusion.

cura.roofing_layer_count.label: Top Surface Skin Layers
cura.roofing_layer_count.tooltip: The number of top most skin layers. Usually only one top most layer is sufficient to generate higher quality top surfaces.

cura.roofing_line_width.label: Top Surface Skin Line Width
cura.roofing_line_width.tooltip: Width of a single line of the areas at the top of the print.

cura.roofing_pattern.label: Top Surface Skin Pattern
cura.roofing_pattern.tooltip: The pattern of the top most layers.

cura.roofing_monotonic.label: Monotonic Top Surface Order
cura.roofing_monotonic.tooltip: Print top surface lines in an ordering that causes them to always overlap with adjacent lines in a single direction. This takes slightly more time to print, but makes flat surfaces look more consistent.

cura.roofing_angles.label: Top Surface Skin Line Directions
cura.roofing_angles.tooltip: A list of integer line directions to use when the top surface skin layers use the lines or zig zag pattern. Elements from the list are used sequentially as the layers progress and when the end of the list is reached, it starts at the beginning again. The list items are separated by commas and the whole list is contained in square brackets. Default is an empty list which means use the traditional default angles (45 and 135 degrees).

cura.roofing_expansion.label: Top Surface Expansion
cura.roofing_expansion.tooltip: Determines how much the top surfaces are expanded beneath overlapping surfaces. By adjusting this value, you can ensure that the outer edges of the top surfaces are concealed by the layers above, resulting in a better visual quality, particularly for models with curved surfaces.

cura.flooring_extruder_nr.label: Bottom Surface Skin Extruder
cura.flooring_extruder_nr.tooltip: The extruder train used for printing the bottom most skin. This is used in multi-extrusion.

cura.flooring_layer_count.label: Bottom Surface Skin Layers
cura.flooring_layer_count.tooltip: The number of bottom most skin layers. Usually only one bottom most layer is sufficient to generate higher quality bottom surfaces.

cura.flooring_line_width.label: Bottom Surface Skin Line Width
cura.flooring_line_width.tooltip: Width of a single line of the areas at the bottom of the print.

cura.flooring_pattern.label: Bottom Surface Skin Pattern
cura.flooring_pattern.tooltip: The pattern of the bottom most layers.

cura.flooring_monotonic.label: Monotonic Bottom Surface Order
cura.flooring_monotonic.tooltip: Print bottom surface lines in an ordering that causes them to always overlap with adjacent lines in a single direction. This takes slightly more time to print, but makes flat surfaces look more consistent.

cura.flooring_angles.label: Bottom Surface Skin Line Directions
cura.flooring_angles.tooltip: A list of integer line directions to use when the bottom surface skin layers use the lines or zig zag pattern. Elements from the list are used sequentially as the layers progress and when the end of the list is reached, it starts at the beginning again. The list items are separated by commas and the whole list is contained in square brackets. Default is an empty list which means use the traditional default angles (45 and 135 degrees).

cura.top_bottom_extruder_nr.label: Top/Bottom Extruder
cura.top_bottom_extruder_nr.tooltip: The extruder train used for printing the top and bottom skin. This is used in multi-extrusion.

cura.top_bottom_thickness.label: Top/Bottom Thickness
cura.top_bottom_thickness.tooltip: The thickness of the top/bottom layers in the print. This value divided by the layer height defines the number of top/bottom layers.

cura.initial_bottom_layers.label: Initial Bottom Layers
cura.initial_bottom_layers.tooltip: The number of initial bottom layers, from the build-plate upwards. When calculated by the bottom thickness, this value is rounded to a whole number.

cura.top_bottom_pattern_0.label: Bottom Pattern Initial Layer
cura.top_bottom_pattern_0.tooltip: The pattern on the bottom of the print on the first layer.

cura.top_bottom_skin_merge_distance.label: Top/Bottom/Skin Merge Distance
cura.top_bottom_skin_merge_distance.tooltip: On sloped areas especially, top/bottom can become very small or narrow, while skin is nearby. This will sometimes cause walls not to print well. Merge top/bottom into skin when areas become too thin, where 'too thin' is defined by the merge distance (any thinner is merged into a neighbouring area if present).

cura.connect_skin_polygons.label: Connect Top/Bottom Polygons
cura.connect_skin_polygons.tooltip: Connect top/bottom skin paths where they run next to each other. For the concentric pattern enabling this setting greatly reduces the travel time, but because the connections can happen midway over infill this feature can reduce the top surface quality.

cura.skin_monotonic.label: Monotonic Top/Bottom Order
cura.skin_monotonic.tooltip: Print top/bottom lines in an ordering that causes them to always overlap with adjacent lines in a single direction. This takes slightly more time to print, but makes flat surfaces look more consistent.

cura.skin_angles.label: Top/Bottom Line Directions
cura.skin_angles.tooltip: A list of integer line directions to use when the top/bottom layers use the lines or zig zag pattern. Elements from the list are used sequentially as the layers progress and when the end of the list is reached, it starts at the beginning again. The list items are separated by commas and the whole list is contained in square brackets. Default is an empty list which means use the traditional default angles (45 and 135 degrees).

cura.small_skin_width.label: Small Top/Bottom Width
cura.small_skin_width.tooltip: Small top/bottom regions are filled with walls instead of the default top/bottom pattern. This helps to avoids jerky motions. Off for the topmost (air-exposed) layer by default (see 'Small Top/Bottom On Surface').

cura.small_skin_on_surface.label: Small Top/Bottom On Surface
cura.small_skin_on_surface.tooltip: Enable small (up to 'Small Top/Bottom Width') regions on the topmost skinned layer (exposed to air) to be filled with walls instead of the default pattern.

cura.skin_no_small_gaps_heuristic.label: No Skin in Z Gaps
cura.skin_no_small_gaps_heuristic.tooltip: When the model has small vertical gaps of only a few layers, there should normally be skin around those layers in the narrow space. Enable this setting to not generate skin if the vertical gap is very small. This improves printing time and slicing time, but technically leaves infill exposed to the air.

default.expr: 0 if top_bottom_pattern == 'concentric' and top_bottom_pattern_0 == 'concentric' and roofing_layer_count <= 0 else 1

cura.skin_outline_count.label: Extra Skin Wall Count
cura.skin_outline_count.tooltip: Replaces the outermost part of the top/bottom pattern with a number of concentric lines. Using one or two lines improves roofs that start on infill material.

cura.ironing_only_highest_layer.label: Iron Only Highest Layer
cura.ironing_only_highest_layer.tooltip: Only perform ironing on the very last layer of the mesh. This saves time if the lower layers don't need a smooth surface finish.

cura.ironing_monotonic.label: Monotonic Ironing Order
cura.ironing_monotonic.tooltip: Print ironing lines in an ordering that causes them to always overlap with adjacent lines in a single direction. This takes slightly more time to print, but makes flat surfaces look more consistent.

cura.acceleration_ironing.label: Ironing Acceleration
cura.acceleration_ironing.tooltip: The acceleration with which ironing is performed.

cura.jerk_ironing.label: Ironing Jerk
cura.jerk_ironing.tooltip: The maximum instantaneous velocity change while performing ironing.

default.expr: 0.5 * (skin_line_width + (wall_line_width_x if wall_line_count > 1 else wall_line_width_0)) * skin_overlap / 100 if top_bottom_pattern != 'concentric' else 0

cura.skin_overlap_mm.label: Skin Overlap
cura.skin_overlap_mm.tooltip: Adjust the amount of overlap between the walls and (the endpoints of) the skin-centerlines. A slight overlap allows the walls to connect firmly to the skin. Note that, given an equal skin and wall line-width, any value over half the width of the wall may already cause any skin to go past the wall, because at that point the position of the nozzle of the skin-extruder may already reach past the middle of the wall.

cura.skin_preshrink.label: Skin Removal Width
cura.skin_preshrink.tooltip: The largest width of skin areas which are to be removed. Every skin area smaller than this value will disappear. This can help in limiting the amount of time and material spent on printing top/bottom skin at slanted surfaces in the model.

cura.top_skin_preshrink.label: Top Skin Removal Width
cura.top_skin_preshrink.tooltip: The largest width of top skin areas which are to be removed. Every skin area smaller than this value will disappear. This can help in limiting the amount of time and material spent on printing top skin at slanted surfaces in the model.

cura.bottom_skin_preshrink.label: Bottom Skin Removal Width
cura.bottom_skin_preshrink.tooltip: The largest width of bottom skin areas which are to be removed. Every skin area smaller than this value will disappear. This can help in limiting the amount of time and material spent on printing bottom skin at slanted surfaces in the model.

cura.expand_skins_expand_distance.label: Skin Expand Distance
cura.expand_skins_expand_distance.tooltip: The distance the skins are expanded into the infill. Higher values makes the skin attach better to the infill pattern and makes the walls on neighboring layers adhere better to the skin. Lower values save amount of material used.

cura.top_skin_expand_distance.label: Top Skin Expand Distance
cura.top_skin_expand_distance.tooltip: The distance the top skins are expanded into the infill. Higher values makes the skin attach better to the infill pattern and makes the walls on the layer above adhere better to the skin. Lower values save amount of material used.

cura.bottom_skin_expand_distance.label: Bottom Skin Expand Distance
cura.bottom_skin_expand_distance.tooltip: The distance the bottom skins are expanded into the infill. Higher values makes the skin attach better to the infill pattern and makes the skin adhere better to the walls on the layer below. Lower values save amount of material used.

cura.max_skin_angle_for_expansion.label: Maximum Skin Angle for Expansion
cura.max_skin_angle_for_expansion.tooltip: Top and/or bottom surfaces of your object with an angle larger than this setting, won't have their top/bottom skin expanded. This avoids expanding the narrow skin areas that are created when the model surface has a near vertical slope. An angle of 0° is horizontal and will cause no skin to be expanded, while an angle of 90° is vertical and will cause all skin to be expanded.

cura.min_skin_width_for_expansion.label: Minimum Skin Width for Expansion
cura.min_skin_width_for_expansion.tooltip: Skin areas narrower than this are not expanded. This avoids expanding the narrow skin areas that are created when the model surface has a slope close to the vertical.

cura.infill_extruder_nr.label: Infill Extruder
cura.infill_extruder_nr.tooltip: The extruder train used for printing infill. This is used in multi-extrusion.

default.expr: 0 if infill_sparse_density == 0 else (((infill_line_width * 100) / infill_sparse_density) * (((4/3) - (1/3) * (infill_sparse_density / 100.0)) if infill_pattern in ['honeycomb', 'octagon'] else (2 if infill_pattern == 'grid' else (3 if infill_pattern in ['triangles', 'trihexagon', 'cubic', 'cubicsubdiv'] else (2 if infill_pattern in ['tetrahedral', 'quarter_cubic'] else (1 if infill_pattern in ['cross', 'cross_3d'] else (1.6 if infill_pattern == 'lightning' else 1)))))))

cura.infill_line_distance.label: Infill Line Distance
cura.infill_line_distance.tooltip: Distance between the printed infill lines. This setting is calculated by the infill density and the infill line width.

cura.zig_zaggify_infill.label: Connect Infill Lines
cura.zig_zaggify_infill.tooltip: Connect the ends where the infill pattern meets the inner wall using a line which follows the shape of the inner wall. Enabling this setting can make the infill adhere to the walls better and reduce the effects of infill on the quality of vertical surfaces. Disabling this setting reduces the amount of material used.

default.expr: (infill_pattern == 'cross' or infill_pattern == 'cross_3d' or infill_multiplier % 2 == 0) and infill_wall_line_count > 0

cura.connect_infill_polygons.label: Connect Infill Polygons
cura.connect_infill_polygons.tooltip: Connect infill paths where they run next to each other. For infill patterns which consist of several closed polygons, enabling this setting greatly reduces the travel time.

default.expr: [0, 90] if infill_pattern == 'octagon' else [0, 60, 120] if infill_pattern == 'honeycomb' else [0] if infill_pattern == 'gyroid' else [ ]

cura.infill_angles.label: Infill Line Directions
cura.infill_angles.tooltip: A list of integer line directions to use. Elements from the list are used sequentially as the layers progress and when the end of the list is reached, it starts at the beginning again. The list items are separated by commas and the whole list is contained in square brackets. Default is an empty list which means use the traditional default angles (45 and 135 degrees for the lines and zig zag patterns and 45 degrees for all other patterns).

cura.infill_offset_x.label: Infill X Offset
cura.infill_offset_x.tooltip: The infill pattern is moved this distance along the X axis.

cura.infill_offset_y.label: Infill Y Offset
cura.infill_offset_y.tooltip: The infill pattern is moved this distance along the Y axis.

cura.infill_multiplier.label: Infill Line Multiplier
cura.infill_multiplier.tooltip: Convert each infill line to this many lines. The extra lines do not cross over each other, but avoid each other. This makes the infill stiffer, but increases print time and material usage.

cura.infill_wall_line_count.label: Extra Infill Wall Count
cura.infill_wall_line_count.tooltip:
Add extra walls around the infill area. Such walls can make top/bottom skin lines sag down less which means you need less top/bottom skin layers for the same quality at the cost of some extra material.
This feature can combine with the Connect Infill Polygons to connect all the infill into a single extrusion path without the need for travels or retractions if configured right.

cura.sub_div_rad_add.label: Cubic Subdivision Shell
cura.sub_div_rad_add.tooltip: An addition to the radius from the center of each cube to check for the boundary of the model, as to decide whether this cube should be subdivided. Larger values lead to a thicker shell of small cubes near the boundary of the model.

default.expr: 0.5 * (infill_line_width + (wall_line_width_x if wall_line_count > 1 else wall_line_width_0)) * infill_overlap / 100 if infill_sparse_density < 95 and infill_pattern != 'concentric' else 0

cura.infill_overlap_mm.label: Infill Overlap
cura.infill_overlap_mm.tooltip: The amount of overlap between the infill and the walls. A slight overlap allows the walls to connect firmly to the infill.

cura.infill_wipe_dist.label: Infill Wipe Distance
cura.infill_wipe_dist.tooltip: Distance of a travel move inserted after every infill line, to make the infill stick to the walls better. This option is similar to infill overlap, but without extrusion and only on one end of the infill line.

cura.infill_sparse_thickness.label: Infill Layer Thickness
cura.infill_sparse_thickness.tooltip: The thickness per layer of infill material. This value should always be a multiple of the layer height and is otherwise rounded.

cura.gradual_infill_steps.label: Gradual Infill Steps
cura.gradual_infill_steps.tooltip: Number of times to reduce the infill density by half when getting further below top surfaces. Areas which are closer to top surfaces get a higher density, up to the Infill Density.

cura.gradual_infill_step_height.label: Gradual Infill Step Height
cura.gradual_infill_step_height.tooltip: The height of infill of a given density before switching to half the density.

cura.min_infill_area.label: Minimum Infill Area
cura.min_infill_area.tooltip: Don't generate areas of infill smaller than this (use skin instead).

cura.infill_support_enabled.label: Infill Support
cura.infill_support_enabled.tooltip: Print infill structures only where tops of the model should be supported. Enabling this reduces print time and material usage, but leads to ununiform object strength.

cura.infill_support_angle.label: Infill Overhang Angle
cura.infill_support_angle.tooltip: The minimum angle of internal overhangs for which infill is added. At a value of 0° objects are totally filled with infill, 90° will not provide any infill.

default.expr: infill_sparse_density < 40 and gradual_infill_steps == 0 and infill_sparse_thickness == layer_height

cura.skin_support.label: Infill Skin Support
cura.skin_support.tooltip: Print a solid infill pattern just below skin to avoid printing the skin over air.

cura.skin_support_speed.label: Skin Support Speed
cura.skin_support_speed.tooltip: The speed at which skin support regions are printed.

cura.skin_support_material_flow.label: Skin Support Flow
cura.skin_support_material_flow.tooltip: When printing skin support regions, the amount of material extruded is multiplied by this value.

cura.skin_support_density.label: Skin Support Density
cura.skin_support_density.tooltip: The density of the skin support layer. Values less than 100 will increase the gaps between the lines.

cura.skin_support_fan_speed.label: Skin Support Fan Speed
cura.skin_support_fan_speed.tooltip: Percentage fan speed to use when printing skin support.

cura.skin_support_interlace_lines.label: Interlace Skin Support Lines
cura.skin_support_interlace_lines.tooltip: When enabled, skin support lines will be printed interlaced, i.e. in 2 monotonic passes so that adjacent lines won't be printed just after each other. The lines of the first pass then have more time to cool down and are stronger when the second pass is added.

cura.lightning_infill_support_angle.label: Lightning Infill Support Angle
cura.lightning_infill_support_angle.tooltip: Determines when a lightning infill layer has to support anything above it. Measured in the angle given the thickness of a layer.

cura.lightning_infill_overhang_angle.label: Lightning Infill Overhang Angle
cura.lightning_infill_overhang_angle.tooltip: Determines when a lightning infill layer has to support the model above it. Measured in the angle given the thickness.

cura.lightning_infill_prune_angle.label: Lightning Infill Prune Angle
cura.lightning_infill_prune_angle.tooltip: The endpoints of infill lines are shortened to save on material. This setting is the angle of overhang of the endpoints of these lines.

cura.lightning_infill_straightening_angl.label: Lightning Infill Straightening Angle
cura.lightning_infill_straightening_angl.tooltip: The infill lines are straightened out to save on printing time. This is the maximum angle of overhang allowed across the length of the infill line.

cura.infill_move_inwards_length.label: Infill Start/End Move Inwards Length
cura.infill_move_inwards_length.tooltip: When starting or ending infill print, add an inwards extrusion move so that the tips of the infill won't impact the outer wall. This can be useful when the infill is printed at very high speed.

cura.infill_start_move_inwards_length.label: Infill Start Move Inwards Length
cura.infill_start_move_inwards_length.tooltip: When starting infill print, add an inwards extrusion move so that the tips of the infill won't impact the outer wall. This can be useful when the infill is printed at very high speed.

cura.infill_end_move_inwards_length.label: Infill End Move Inwards Length
cura.infill_end_move_inwards_length.tooltip: When starting or ending infill print, add an inwards extrusion move so that the tips of the infill won't impact the outer wall. This can be useful when the infill is printed at very high speed.

cura.infill_start_end_preference.label: Infill Start/End Preference
cura.infill_start_end_preference.tooltip:
• Start at closest: Infill will start at the position that is the closest to the previous position.
  • Start at random: Use a random position for each infill area. This prevents one segment becoming the strongest, but it does so at the cost of an additional travel move.
  • End close to seam: the infill lines will be ordered so that they end as close as possible to the next wall seam. If required, an infill line will be split to provide an appropriate ending position. This helps shortening the travel move between the infill and the wall start position, which should provide a better wall seam, at the cost of adding travel moves during infill print.
    ℹ️ Note that this will be applied only when walls are printed just after infill.

cura.default_material_print_temperature.label: Default Printing Temperature
cura.default_material_print_temperature.tooltip: The default temperature used for printing. This should be the "base" temperature of a material. All other print temperatures should use offsets based on this value

cura.material_initial_print_temperature.label: Initial Printing Temperature
cura.material_initial_print_temperature.tooltip: The minimal temperature while heating up to the Printing Temperature at which printing can already start.

cura.material_final_print_temperature.label: Final Printing Temperature
cura.material_final_print_temperature.tooltip: The temperature to which to already start cooling down just before the end of printing.

cura.material_extrusion_cool_down_speed.label: Extrusion Cool Down Speed Modifier
cura.material_extrusion_cool_down_speed.tooltip: The extra speed by which the nozzle cools while extruding. The same value is used to signify the heat up speed lost when heating up while extruding.

cura.default_material_bed_temperature.label: Default Build Plate Temperature
cura.default_material_bed_temperature.tooltip: The default temperature used for the heated build plate. This should be the "base" temperature of a build plate. All other print temperatures should use offsets based on this value

cura.material_shrinkage_percentage.label: Scaling Factor Shrinkage Compensation
cura.material_shrinkage_percentage.tooltip: To compensate for the shrinkage of the material as it cools down, the model will be scaled with this factor.

cura.material_shrinkage_percentage_xy.label: Horizontal Scaling Factor Shrinkage Compensation
cura.material_shrinkage_percentage_xy.tooltip: To compensate for the shrinkage of the material as it cools down, the model will be scaled with this factor in the XY-direction (horizontally).

cura.material_shrinkage_percentage_z.label: Vertical Scaling Factor Shrinkage Compensation
cura.material_shrinkage_percentage_z.tooltip: To compensate for the shrinkage of the material as it cools down, the model will be scaled with this factor in the Z-direction (vertically).

cura.material_crystallinity.label: Crystalline Material
cura.material_crystallinity.tooltip: Is this material the type that breaks off cleanly when heated (crystalline), or is it the type that produces long intertwined polymer chains (non-crystalline)?

cura.material_anti_ooze_retracted_positi.label: Anti-ooze Retracted Position
cura.material_anti_ooze_retracted_positi.tooltip: How far the material needs to be retracted before it stops oozing.

cura.material_anti_ooze_retraction_speed.label: Anti-ooze Retraction Speed
cura.material_anti_ooze_retraction_speed.tooltip: How fast the material needs to be retracted during a filament switch to prevent oozing.

cura.material_break_preparation_retracte.label: Break Preparation Retracted Position
cura.material_break_preparation_retracte.tooltip: How far the filament can be stretched before it breaks, while heated.

cura.material_break_preparation_speed.label: Break Preparation Retraction Speed
cura.material_break_preparation_speed.tooltip: How fast the filament needs to be retracted just before breaking it off in a retraction.

cura.material_break_preparation_temperat.label: Break Preparation Temperature
cura.material_break_preparation_temperat.tooltip: The temperature used to purge material, should be roughly equal to the highest possible printing temperature.

cura.material_break_retracted_position.label: Break Retracted Position
cura.material_break_retracted_position.tooltip: How far to retract the filament in order to break it cleanly.

cura.material_break_speed.label: Break Retraction Speed
cura.material_break_speed.tooltip: The speed at which to retract the filament in order to break it cleanly.

cura.material_break_temperature.label: Break Temperature
cura.material_break_temperature.tooltip: The temperature at which the filament is broken for a clean break.

cura.material_flush_purge_speed.label: Flush Purge Speed
cura.material_flush_purge_speed.tooltip: How fast to prime the material after switching to a different material.

cura.material_flush_purge_length.label: Flush Purge Length
cura.material_flush_purge_length.tooltip: How much material to use to purge the previous material out of the nozzle (in length of filament) when switching to a different material.

cura.material_end_of_filament_purge_spee.label: End of Filament Purge Speed
cura.material_end_of_filament_purge_spee.tooltip: How fast to prime the material after replacing an empty spool with a fresh spool of the same material.

cura.material_end_of_filament_purge_leng.label: End of Filament Purge Length
cura.material_end_of_filament_purge_leng.tooltip: How much material to use to purge the previous material out of the nozzle (in length of filament) when replacing an empty spool with a fresh spool of the same material.

cura.material_maximum_park_duration.label: Maximum Park Duration
cura.material_maximum_park_duration.tooltip: How long the material can be kept out of dry storage safely.

cura.material_no_load_move_factor.label: No Load Move Factor
cura.material_no_load_move_factor.tooltip: A factor indicating how much the filament gets compressed between the feeder and the nozzle chamber, used to determine how far to move the material for a filament switch.

cura.wall_0_material_flow.label: Outer Wall Flow
cura.wall_0_material_flow.tooltip: Flow compensation on the outermost wall line.

cura.wall_x_material_flow.label: Inner Wall(s) Flow
cura.wall_x_material_flow.tooltip: Flow compensation on wall lines for all wall lines except the outermost one.

cura.wall_0_material_flow_roofing.label: Top Surface Outer Wall Flow
cura.wall_0_material_flow_roofing.tooltip: Flow compensation on the top surface outermost wall line.

cura.wall_x_material_flow_roofing.label: Top Surface Inner Wall(s) Flow
cura.wall_x_material_flow_roofing.tooltip: Flow compensation on top surface wall lines for all wall lines except the outermost one.

cura.wall_0_material_flow_flooring.label: Bottom Surface Outer Wall Flow
cura.wall_0_material_flow_flooring.tooltip: Flow compensation on the bottom surface outermost wall line.

cura.wall_x_material_flow_flooring.label: Bottom Surface Inner Wall(s) Flow
cura.wall_x_material_flow_flooring.tooltip: Flow compensation on bottom surface wall lines for all wall lines except the outermost one.

cura.roofing_material_flow.label: Top Surface Skin Flow
cura.roofing_material_flow.tooltip: Flow compensation on lines of the areas at the top of the print.

cura.flooring_material_flow.label: Bottom Surface Skin Flow
cura.flooring_material_flow.tooltip: Flow compensation on lines of the areas at the bottom of the print.

cura.skirt_brim_material_flow.label: Skirt/Brim Flow
cura.skirt_brim_material_flow.tooltip: Flow compensation on skirt or brim lines.

cura.support_material_flow.label: Support Flow
cura.support_material_flow.tooltip: Flow compensation on support structure lines.

cura.support_interface_material_flow.label: Support Interface Flow
cura.support_interface_material_flow.tooltip: Flow compensation on lines of support roof or floor.

cura.support_roof_material_flow.label: Support Roof Flow
cura.support_roof_material_flow.tooltip: Flow compensation on support roof lines.

cura.support_bottom_material_flow.label: Support Floor Flow
cura.support_bottom_material_flow.tooltip: Flow compensation on support floor lines.

cura.prime_tower_flow.label: Prime Tower Flow
cura.prime_tower_flow.tooltip: Flow compensation on prime tower lines.

cura.material_flow_layer_0.label: Initial Layer Flow
cura.material_flow_layer_0.tooltip: Flow compensation for the first layer: the amount of material extruded on the initial layer is multiplied by this value.

cura.wall_x_material_flow_layer_0.label: Initial Layer Inner Wall Flow
cura.wall_x_material_flow_layer_0.tooltip: Flow compensation on wall lines for all wall lines except the outermost one, but only for the first layer

cura.wall_0_material_flow_layer_0.label: Initial Layer Outer Wall Flow
cura.wall_0_material_flow_layer_0.tooltip: Flow compensation on the outermost wall line of the first layer.

cura.skin_material_flow_layer_0.label: Initial Layer Bottom Flow
cura.skin_material_flow_layer_0.tooltip: Flow compensation on bottom lines of the first layer

cura.material_standby_temperature.label: Standby Temperature
cura.material_standby_temperature.tooltip: The temperature of the nozzle when another nozzle is currently used for printing.

cura.material_is_support_material.label: Is support material
cura.material_is_support_material.tooltip: Is this material typically used as a support material during printing.

cura.gradual_flow_enabled.label: Gradual flow enabled
cura.gradual_flow_enabled.tooltip: Enable gradual flow changes. When enabled, the flow is gradually increased/decreased to the target flow. This is useful for printers with a bowden tube where the flow is not immediately changed when the extruder motor starts/stops.

cura.max_flow_acceleration.label: Gradual flow max acceleration
cura.max_flow_acceleration.tooltip: Maximum acceleration for gradual flow changes

cura.layer_0_max_flow_acceleration.label: Initial layer max flow acceleration
cura.layer_0_max_flow_acceleration.tooltip: Minimum speed for gradual flow changes for the first layer

cura.gradual_flow_discretisation_step_si.label: Gradual flow discretisation step size
cura.gradual_flow_discretisation_step_si.tooltip: Duration of each step in the gradual flow change

cura.material_pressure_advance_factor.label: Pressure advance factor
cura.material_pressure_advance_factor.tooltip: Tuning factor for pressure advance, which is meant to synchronize extrusion with motion

cura.material_max_flowrate.label: Material Maximum Flow Rate
cura.material_max_flowrate.tooltip: Maximum flow rate that the printer can extrude for the material

cura.speed_print.label: Print Speed
cura.speed_print.tooltip: The speed at which printing happens.

cura.speed_wall.label: Wall Speed
cura.speed_wall.tooltip: The speed at which the walls are printed.

cura.speed_wall_0_roofing.label: Top Surface Outer Wall Speed
cura.speed_wall_0_roofing.tooltip: The speed at which the top surface outermost wall is printed.

cura.speed_wall_x_roofing.label: Top Surface Inner Wall Speed
cura.speed_wall_x_roofing.tooltip: The speed at which the top surface inner walls are printed.

cura.speed_wall_0_flooring.label: Bottom Surface Outer Wall Speed
cura.speed_wall_0_flooring.tooltip: The speed at which the bottom surface outermost wall is printed.

cura.speed_wall_x_flooring.label: Bottom Surface Inner Wall Speed
cura.speed_wall_x_flooring.tooltip: The speed at which the bottom surface inner walls are printed.

cura.speed_roofing.label: Top Surface Skin Speed
cura.speed_roofing.tooltip: The speed at which top surface skin layers are printed.

cura.speed_flooring.label: Bottom Surface Skin Speed
cura.speed_flooring.tooltip: The speed at which bottom surface skin layers are printed.

cura.speed_support_infill.label: Support Infill Speed
cura.speed_support_infill.tooltip: The speed at which the infill of support is printed. Printing the infill at lower speeds improves stability.

cura.speed_support_roof.label: Support Roof Speed
cura.speed_support_roof.tooltip: The speed at which the roofs of support are printed. Printing them at lower speeds can improve overhang quality.

cura.speed_support_bottom.label: Support Floor Speed
cura.speed_support_bottom.tooltip: The speed at which the floor of support is printed. Printing it at lower speed can improve adhesion of support on top of your model.

cura.speed_prime_tower.label: Prime Tower Speed
cura.speed_prime_tower.tooltip: The speed at which the prime tower is printed. Printing the prime tower slower can make it more stable when the adhesion between the different filaments is suboptimal.

cura.speed_print_layer_0.label: Initial Layer Print Speed
cura.speed_print_layer_0.tooltip: The speed of printing for the initial layer. A lower value is advised to improve adhesion to the build plate.

cura.speed_travel_layer_0.label: Initial Layer Travel Speed
cura.speed_travel_layer_0.tooltip: The speed of travel moves in the initial layer. A lower value is advised to prevent pulling previously printed parts away from the build plate. The value of this setting can automatically be calculated from the ratio between the Travel Speed and the Print Speed.

cura.speed_slowdown_layers.label: Number of Slower Layers
cura.speed_slowdown_layers.tooltip: The first few layers are printed slower than the rest of the model, to get better adhesion to the build plate and improve the overall success rate of prints. The speed is gradually increased over these layers.

cura.speed_equalize_flow_width_factor.label: Flow Equalization Ratio
cura.speed_equalize_flow_width_factor.tooltip: Extrusion width based correction factor on the speed. At 0% the movement speed is kept constant at the Print Speed. At 100% the movement speed is adjusted so that the flow (in mm³/s) is kept constant, i.e. lines half the normal Line Width are printed twice as fast and lines twice as wide are printed half as fast. A value larger than 100% can help to compensate for the higher pressure required to extrude wide lines.

cura.acceleration_enabled.label: Enable Acceleration Control
cura.acceleration_enabled.tooltip: Enables adjusting the print head acceleration. Increasing the accelerations can reduce printing time at the cost of print quality.

cura.acceleration_travel_enabled.label: Enable Travel Acceleration
cura.acceleration_travel_enabled.tooltip: Use a separate acceleration rate for travel moves. If disabled, travel moves will use the acceleration value of the printed line at their destination.

cura.acceleration_wall.label: Wall Acceleration
cura.acceleration_wall.tooltip: The acceleration with which the walls are printed.

cura.acceleration_wall_0_roofing.label: Top Surface Outer Wall Acceleration
cura.acceleration_wall_0_roofing.tooltip: The acceleration with which the top surface outermost walls are printed.

cura.acceleration_wall_x_roofing.label: Top Surface Inner Wall Acceleration
cura.acceleration_wall_x_roofing.tooltip: The acceleration with which the top surface inner walls are printed.

cura.acceleration_wall_0_flooring.label: Bottom Surface Outer Wall Acceleration
cura.acceleration_wall_0_flooring.tooltip: The acceleration with which the bottom surface outermost walls are printed.

cura.acceleration_wall_x_flooring.label: Bottom Surface Inner Wall Acceleration
cura.acceleration_wall_x_flooring.tooltip: The acceleration with which the bottom surface inner walls are printed.

cura.acceleration_roofing.label: Top Surface Skin Acceleration
cura.acceleration_roofing.tooltip: The acceleration with which top surface skin layers are printed.

cura.acceleration_flooring.label: Bottom Surface Skin Acceleration
cura.acceleration_flooring.tooltip: The acceleration with which bottom surface skin layers are printed.

cura.acceleration_support.label: Support Acceleration
cura.acceleration_support.tooltip: The acceleration with which the support structure is printed.

cura.acceleration_support_infill.label: Support Infill Acceleration
cura.acceleration_support_infill.tooltip: The acceleration with which the infill of support is printed.

cura.acceleration_support_interface.label: Support Interface Acceleration
cura.acceleration_support_interface.tooltip: The acceleration with which the roofs and floors of support are printed. Printing them at lower acceleration can improve overhang quality.

cura.acceleration_support_roof.label: Support Roof Acceleration
cura.acceleration_support_roof.tooltip: The acceleration with which the roofs of support are printed. Printing them at lower acceleration can improve overhang quality.

cura.acceleration_support_bottom.label: Support Floor Acceleration
cura.acceleration_support_bottom.tooltip: The acceleration with which the floors of support are printed. Printing them at lower acceleration can improve adhesion of support on top of your model.

cura.acceleration_prime_tower.label: Prime Tower Acceleration
cura.acceleration_prime_tower.tooltip: The acceleration with which the prime tower is printed.

cura.acceleration_print_layer_0.label: Initial Layer Print Acceleration
cura.acceleration_print_layer_0.tooltip: The acceleration during the printing of the initial layer.

cura.acceleration_travel_layer_0.label: Initial Layer Travel Acceleration
cura.acceleration_travel_layer_0.tooltip: The acceleration for travel moves in the initial layer.

cura.acceleration_skirt_brim.label: Skirt/Brim Acceleration
cura.acceleration_skirt_brim.tooltip: The acceleration with which the skirt and brim are printed. Normally this is done with the initial layer acceleration, but sometimes you might want to print the skirt or brim at a different acceleration.

cura.jerk_enabled.label: Enable Jerk Control
cura.jerk_enabled.tooltip: Enables adjusting the jerk of print head when the velocity in the X or Y axis changes. Increasing the jerk can reduce printing time at the cost of print quality.

cura.jerk_travel_enabled.label: Enable Travel Jerk
cura.jerk_travel_enabled.tooltip: Use a separate jerk rate for travel moves. If disabled, travel moves will use the jerk value of the printed line at their destination.

cura.jerk_wall.label: Wall Jerk
cura.jerk_wall.tooltip: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which the walls are printed.

cura.jerk_wall_0_roofing.label: Top Surface Outer Wall Jerk
cura.jerk_wall_0_roofing.tooltip: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which the top surface outermost walls are printed.

cura.jerk_wall_x_roofing.label: Top Surface Inner Wall Jerk
cura.jerk_wall_x_roofing.tooltip: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which the top surface inner walls are printed.

cura.jerk_wall_0_flooring.label: Bottom Surface Outer Wall Jerk
cura.jerk_wall_0_flooring.tooltip: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which the bottom surface outermost walls are printed.

cura.jerk_wall_x_flooring.label: Bottom Surface Inner Wall Jerk
cura.jerk_wall_x_flooring.tooltip: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which the bottom surface inner walls are printed.

cura.jerk_roofing.label: Top Surface Skin Jerk
cura.jerk_roofing.tooltip: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which top surface skin layers are printed.

cura.jerk_flooring.label: Bottom Surface Skin Jerk
cura.jerk_flooring.tooltip: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which bottom surface skin layers are printed.

cura.jerk_support.label: Support Jerk
cura.jerk_support.tooltip: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which the support structure is printed.

cura.jerk_support_infill.label: Support Infill Jerk
cura.jerk_support_infill.tooltip: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which the infill of support is printed.

cura.jerk_support_interface.label: Support Interface Jerk
cura.jerk_support_interface.tooltip: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which the roofs and floors of support are printed.

cura.jerk_support_roof.label: Support Roof Jerk
cura.jerk_support_roof.tooltip: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which the roofs of support are printed.

cura.jerk_support_bottom.label: Support Floor Jerk
cura.jerk_support_bottom.tooltip: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which the floors of support are printed.

cura.jerk_prime_tower.label: Prime Tower Jerk
cura.jerk_prime_tower.tooltip: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which the prime tower is printed.

cura.jerk_print_layer_0.label: Initial Layer Print Jerk
cura.jerk_print_layer_0.tooltip: The maximum instantaneous velocity change during the printing of the initial layer.

cura.jerk_travel_layer_0.label: Initial Layer Travel Jerk
cura.jerk_travel_layer_0.tooltip: The acceleration for travel moves in the initial layer.

cura.jerk_skirt_brim.label: Skirt/Brim Jerk
cura.jerk_skirt_brim.tooltip: The maximum instantaneous velocity change with which the skirt and brim are printed.

cura.retraction_enable.label: Enable Retraction
cura.retraction_enable.tooltip: Retract the filament when the nozzle is moving over a non-printed area.

cura.retraction_retract_speed.label: Retraction Retract Speed
cura.retraction_retract_speed.tooltip: The speed at which the filament is retracted during a retraction move.

cura.retraction_count_max.label: Maximum Retraction Count
cura.retraction_count_max.tooltip: This setting limits the number of retractions occurring within the minimum extrusion distance window. Further retractions within this window will be ignored. This avoids retracting repeatedly on the same piece of filament, as that can flatten the filament and cause grinding issues.

cura.retraction_extrusion_window.label: Minimum Extrusion Distance Window
cura.retraction_extrusion_window.tooltip: The window in which the maximum retraction count is enforced. This value should be approximately the same as the retraction distance, so that effectively the number of times a retraction passes the same patch of material is limited.

default.expr: 'no_outer_surfaces' if (any(extruderValues('skin_monotonic')) or any(extruderValues('ironing_enabled')) or (any(extruderValues('roofing_monotonic')) and any(extruderValues('roofing_layer_count')))) else 'all'

cura.retraction_combing.label: Combing Mode
cura.retraction_combing.tooltip: Combing keeps the nozzle within already printed areas when traveling. This results in slightly longer travel moves but reduces the need for retractions. If combing is off, the material will retract and the nozzle moves in a straight line to the next point. It is also possible to avoid combing over top/bottom skin areas or to only comb within the infill.

cura.retraction_combing_max_distance.label: Max Comb Distance With No Retract
cura.retraction_combing_max_distance.tooltip: When greater than zero, combing travel moves that are longer than this distance will use retraction. If set to zero, there is no maximum and combing moves will not use retraction.

cura.retraction_combing_avoid_distance.label: Inside Travel Avoid Distance
cura.retraction_combing_avoid_distance.tooltip: The distance between the nozzle and outer walls when travelling inside a model.

cura.travel_retract_before_outer_wall.label: Retract Before Outer Wall
cura.travel_retract_before_outer_wall.tooltip:
Retraction behavior when moving to the start of an outer wall:
  • Automatic: Retraction will be calculated according to other settings
  • Always: All the travel moves to outer walls will be retracted
  • Never: All the travel moves to outer walls will not be retracted
  • From infill unretracted: The travel move from an infill area to an outer wall will be unretracted, others will use automatic

cura.travel_avoid_other_parts.label: Avoid Printed Parts When Traveling
cura.travel_avoid_other_parts.tooltip: The nozzle avoids already printed parts when traveling. This option is only available when combing is enabled.

cura.travel_avoid_supports.label: Avoid Supports When Traveling
cura.travel_avoid_supports.tooltip: The nozzle avoids already printed supports when traveling. This option is only available when combing is enabled.

cura.travel_avoid_distance.label: Travel Avoid Distance
cura.travel_avoid_distance.tooltip: The distance between the nozzle and already printed parts when avoiding during travel moves.

cura.layer_start_at_z_seam.label: Layer Start at Z Seam
cura.layer_start_at_z_seam.tooltip: Start printing at the Z seam position.

default.expr: (z_seam_x + machine_width / 2 if (not machine_center_is_zero and z_seam_relative) else z_seam_x) if (layer_start_at_z_seam and z_seam_type == 'back') else (sum(extruderValues('machine_extruder_start_pos_x')) / len(extruderValues('machine_extruder_start_pos_x')))

cura.layer_start_x.label: Layer Start X
cura.layer_start_x.tooltip: The X coordinate of the position near where to find the part to start printing each layer.

default.expr: (z_seam_y + machine_depth / 2 if (not machine_center_is_zero and z_seam_relative) else z_seam_y) if (layer_start_at_z_seam and z_seam_type == 'back') else (sum(extruderValues('machine_extruder_start_pos_y')) / len(extruderValues('machine_extruder_start_pos_y')))

cura.layer_start_y.label: Layer Start Y
cura.layer_start_y.tooltip: The Y coordinate of the position near where to find the part to start printing each layer.

cura.retraction_hop_enabled.label: Z Hop When Retracted
cura.retraction_hop_enabled.tooltip: Whenever a retraction is done, the build plate is lowered to create clearance between the nozzle and the print. It prevents the nozzle from hitting the print during travel moves, reducing the chance to knock the print from the build plate.

cura.retraction_hop_only_when_collides.label: Z Hop Only Over Printed Parts
cura.retraction_hop_only_when_collides.tooltip: Only perform a Z Hop when moving over printed parts which cannot be avoided by horizontal motion by Avoid Printed Parts when Traveling.

cura.retraction_hop_after_extruder_switc.label: Z Hop After Extruder Switch
cura.retraction_hop_after_extruder_switc.tooltip: After the machine switched from one extruder to the other, the build plate is lowered to create clearance between the nozzle and the print. This prevents the nozzle from leaving oozed material on the outside of a print.

cura.retraction_hop_after_extruder_switc.label: Z Hop After Extruder Switch Height
cura.retraction_hop_after_extruder_switc.tooltip: The height difference when performing a Z Hop after extruder switch.

cura.cool_fan_enabled.label: Enable Print Cooling
cura.cool_fan_enabled.tooltip: Enables the print cooling fans while printing. The fans improve print quality on layers with short layer times and bridging / overhangs.

cura.build_fan_full_at_height.label: Build Volume Fan Speed at Height
cura.build_fan_full_at_height.tooltip: The height at which the fans spin on regular fan speed. At the layers below the fan speed gradually increases from Initial Fan Speed to Regular Fan Speed.

cura.build_fan_full_layer.label: Build Volume Fan Speed at Layer
cura.build_fan_full_layer.tooltip: The layer at which the build-volume fans spin on full fan speed. This value is calculated and rounded to a whole number.

cura.build_volume_fan_speed_0.label: Initial Layers Build Volume Fan Speed
cura.build_volume_fan_speed_0.tooltip: The fan speed (as a percentage) for the auxiliary or build-volume fan, that is set until the layer specified at 'Build Volume Fan Speed at Layer' is reached. After that, the speed is set by 'Build Volume Fan Speed' instead (so not this 'Initial Layers' one).

cura.build_volume_fan_speed.label: Build Volume Fan Speed
cura.build_volume_fan_speed.tooltip: The fan speed (as a percentage) for the auxiliary or build-volume fan, that is set from the moment that the layer specified at 'Build Volume Fan Speed at Layer' is reached and onwards. Before that, the speed is set by 'Initial Layers Build Volume Fan Speed' instead.

cura.cool_fan_speed.label: Fan Speed
cura.cool_fan_speed.tooltip: The speed at which the print cooling fans spin.

cura.cool_fan_speed_0.label: Initial Fan Speed
cura.cool_fan_speed_0.tooltip: The speed at which the fans spin at the start of the print. In subsequent layers the fan speed is gradually increased up to the layer corresponding to Regular Fan Speed at Height.

cura.cool_fan_full_at_height.label: Regular Fan Speed at Height
cura.cool_fan_full_at_height.tooltip: The height at which the fans spin on regular fan speed. At the layers below the fan speed gradually increases from Initial Fan Speed to Regular Fan Speed.

cura.cool_lift_head.label: Lift Head
cura.cool_lift_head.tooltip: When the minimum speed is hit because of minimum layer time, lift the head away from the print and wait the extra time until the minimum layer time is reached.

cura.cool_min_temperature.label: Small Layer Printing Temperature
cura.cool_min_temperature.tooltip: Gradually reduce to this temperature when printing at reduced speeds because of minimum layer time.

cura.cool_during_extruder_switch.label: Cooling during extruder switch
cura.cool_during_extruder_switch.tooltip:
Whether to activate the cooling fans during a nozzle switch. This can help reducing oozing by cooling the nozzle faster:
  • Unchanged: keep the fans as they were previously
  • Only last extruder: turn on the fan of the last used extruder, but turn the others off (if any). This is useful if you have completely separate extruders.
  • All fans: turn on all fans during nozzle switch. This is useful if you have a single cooling fan, or multiple fans that stay close to each other.

cura.support_extruder_nr.label: Support Extruder
cura.support_extruder_nr.tooltip: The extruder train to use for printing the support. This is used in multi-extrusion.

cura.support_infill_extruder_nr.label: Support Infill Extruder
cura.support_infill_extruder_nr.tooltip: The extruder train to use for printing the infill of the support. This is used in multi-extrusion.

cura.support_extruder_nr_layer_0.label: First Layer Support Extruder
cura.support_extruder_nr_layer_0.tooltip: The extruder train to use for printing the first layer of support infill. This is used in multi-extrusion.

cura.support_interface_extruder_nr.label: Support Interface Extruder
cura.support_interface_extruder_nr.tooltip: The extruder train to use for printing the roofs and floors of the support. This is used in multi-extrusion.

cura.support_roof_extruder_nr.label: Support Roof Extruder
cura.support_roof_extruder_nr.tooltip: The extruder train to use for printing the roofs of the support. This is used in multi-extrusion.

cura.support_bottom_extruder_nr.label: Support Floor Extruder
cura.support_bottom_extruder_nr.tooltip: The extruder train to use for printing the floors of the support. This is used in multi-extrusion.

cura.support_tree_max_diameter.label: Trunk Diameter
cura.support_tree_max_diameter.tooltip: The diameter of the widest branches of tree support. A thicker trunk is more sturdy; a thinner trunk takes up less space on the build plate.

cura.support_tree_smooth_layers.label: Branch Smoothing Layers
cura.support_tree_smooth_layers.tooltip: The positions of the tree support branches will be adjusted to smooth them over the specified number of layers using a rolling window average. This improves inter-layer adhesion and sturdiness, but an excessively high value may cause the structure to bend too close to the model or compromise its integrity.

cura.support_z_seam_away_from_model.label: Support Z Seam Away from Model
cura.support_z_seam_away_from_model.tooltip: Manage the spatial relationship between the z seam of the support structure and the actual 3D model. This control is crucial as it allows users to ensure the seamless removal of support structures post-printing, without inflicting damage or leaving marks on the printed model.

cura.support_z_seam_min_distance.label: Min Z Seam Distance from Model
cura.support_z_seam_min_distance.tooltip: The distance between the model and its support structure at the z-axis seam.

cura.support_type.label: Support Placement
cura.support_type.tooltip: Adjusts the placement of the support structures. The placement can be set to touching build plate or everywhere. When set to everywhere the support structures will also be printed on the model.

cura.support_tree_angle_slow.label: Preferred Branch Angle
cura.support_tree_angle_slow.tooltip: The preferred angle of the branches, when they do not have to avoid the model. Use a lower angle to make them more vertical and more stable. Use a higher angle for branches to merge faster.

cura.support_tree_max_diameter_increase_.label: Diameter Increase To Model
cura.support_tree_max_diameter_increase_.tooltip: The most the diameter of a branch that has to connect to the model may increase by merging with branches that could reach the buildplate. Increasing this reduces print time, but increases the area of support that rests on model

cura.support_tree_min_height_to_model.label: Minimum Height To Model
cura.support_tree_min_height_to_model.tooltip: How tall a branch has to be if it is placed on the model. Prevents small blobs of support. This setting is ignored when a branch is supporting a support roof.

cura.support_tree_bp_diameter.label: Initial Layer Diameter
cura.support_tree_bp_diameter.tooltip: Diameter every branch tries to achieve when reaching the buildplate. Improves bed adhesion.

cura.support_tree_top_rate.label: Branch Density
cura.support_tree_top_rate.tooltip: Adjusts the density of the support structure used to generate the tips of the branches. A higher value results in better overhangs, but the supports are harder to remove. Use Support Roof for very high values or ensure support density is similarly high at the top.

cura.support_tree_limit_branch_reach.label: Limit Branch Reach
cura.support_tree_limit_branch_reach.tooltip: Limit how far each branch should travel from the point it supports. This can make the support more sturdy, but will increase the amount of branches (and because of that material usage/print time)

cura.support_tree_branch_reach_limit.label: Optimal Branch Range
cura.support_tree_branch_reach_limit.tooltip: A recomendation to how far branches can move from the points they support. Branches can violate this value to reach their destination (buildplate or a flat part of the model). Lowering this value will make the support more sturdy, but increase the amount of branches (and because of that material usage/print time)

cura.support_tree_rest_preference.label: Rest Preference
cura.support_tree_rest_preference.tooltip: The preferred placement of the support structures. If structures can't be placed at the preferred location, they will be place elsewhere, even if that means placing them on the model.

default.expr: 1 if support_structure == 'tree' else (1 if (support_pattern == 'grid' or support_pattern == 'triangles' or support_pattern == 'concentric') else 0)

cura.support_wall_count.label: Support Wall Line Count
cura.support_wall_count.tooltip: The number of walls with which to surround support infill. Adding a wall can make support print more reliably and can support overhangs better, but increases print time and material used.

cura.support_wall_thickness.label: Support Wall Thickness
cura.support_wall_thickness.tooltip: The thickness the walls with which to surround support infill. Adding a wall can make support print more reliably and can support overhangs better, but increases print time and material used.

cura.support_enlarged_wall_thickness.label: Support Enlarged Wall Thickness
cura.support_enlarged_wall_thickness.tooltip: The thickness of the walls with which to surround the support infill, when adhesion with the above/below layer is very low. Using larger or extra walls in this case will improve adhesion and make the branch sturdier.

cura.support_wall_thickness_bottom_layer.label: Support Wall Unenlarged Bottom Layers
cura.support_wall_thickness_bottom_layer.tooltip: Number of layers, counted from the build-plate, where support-walls will use the non-enlarged support wall thickness (not accounting for line-width smoothing).

cura.support_wall_thickness_top_layers.label: Support Wall Unenlarged Top Layers
cura.support_wall_thickness_top_layers.tooltip: Number of layers, counted from the closest tip of the branches downwards, where support-walls will use the non-enlarged support wall thickness (not accounting for line-width smoothing).

cura.support_wall_thickness_layer_smooth.label: Support Wall Smooth Layer Width
cura.support_wall_thickness_layer_smooth.tooltip: Number of layers where the support wall line width transition is smoothed out over. (This may still create jumps when one area splits off from the other though.)

cura.support_infill_multiplier.label: Support Infill Line Multiplier
cura.support_infill_multiplier.tooltip: Convert each support infill line to this many lines. The extra lines do not cross over each other, but avoid each other. This makes the infill stiffer, but increases print time and material usage.

cura.support_interface_wall_count.label: Support Interface Wall Line Count
cura.support_interface_wall_count.tooltip: The number of walls with which to surround support interface. Adding a wall can make support print more reliably and can support overhangs better, but increases print time and material used.

cura.support_roof_wall_count.label: Support Roof Wall Line Count
cura.support_roof_wall_count.tooltip: The number of walls with which to surround support interface roof. Adding a wall can make support print more reliably and can support overhangs better, but increases print time and material used.

cura.support_bottom_wall_count.label: Support Bottom Wall Line Count
cura.support_bottom_wall_count.tooltip: The number of walls with which to surround support interface floor. Adding a wall can make support print more reliably and can support overhangs better, but increases print time and material used.

cura.support_lightning_angle.label: Support Lightning Angle
cura.support_lightning_angle.tooltip: Determines when a lightning infill layer has to support anything above it. Measured in the angle given the thickness of a layer.

cura.support_lightning_overhang_angle.label: Support Lightning Overhang Angle
cura.support_lightning_overhang_angle.tooltip: Determines when a lightning infill layer has to support the lines above it. Measured in the angle given the thickness.

cura.support_lightning_prune_angle.label: Support Lightning Prune Angle
cura.support_lightning_prune_angle.tooltip: The endpoints of infill lines are shortened to save on material. This setting is the angle of overhang of the endpoints of these lines.

cura.support_lightning_straightening_ang.label: Support Lightning Straightening Angle
cura.support_lightning_straightening_ang.tooltip: The infill lines are straightened out to save on printing time. This is the maximum angle of overhang allowed across the length of the infill line.

default.expr: support_pattern == 'cross' or support_pattern == 'gyroid' or support_pattern == 'honeycomb' or support_pattern == 'octagon'

cura.zig_zaggify_support.label: Connect Support Lines
cura.zig_zaggify_support.tooltip: Connect the ends of the support lines together. Enabling this setting can make your support more sturdy and reduce underextrusion, but it will cost more material.

cura.support_connect_zigzags.label: Connect Support ZigZags
cura.support_connect_zigzags.tooltip: Connect the ZigZags. This will increase the strength of the zig zag support structure.

cura.support_infill_rate.label: Support Density
cura.support_infill_rate.tooltip: Adjusts the density of the support structure. A higher value results in better overhangs, but the supports are harder to remove.
