cura.support_initial_layer_line_distance.label: Initial Layer Support Line Distance
cura.support_initial_layer_line_distance.tooltip: Distance between the printed initial layer support structure lines. This setting is calculated by the support density.

cura.support_infill_density_multiplier_i.label: Support Infill Density Multiplier Initial Layer
cura.support_infill_density_multiplier_i.tooltip: Multiplier for the infill on the initial layers of the support. Increasing this may help for bed adhesion.

cura.support_infill_angles.label: Support Infill Line Directions
cura.support_infill_angles.tooltip: A list of integer line directions to use. Elements from the list are used sequentially as the layers progress and when the end of the list is reached, it starts at the beginning again. The list items are separated by commas and the whole list is contained in square brackets. Default is an empty list which means use the default angle 0 degrees.

cura.support_brim_enable.label: Enable Inner Support Base
cura.support_brim_enable.tooltip: Generate a base within the support infill regions of the first layers. Enabling this setting increases the adhesion of support to the build plate.

cura.support_outer_brim_enable.label: Enable Outer Support Base
cura.support_outer_brim_enable.tooltip: Generate a base around the support infill regions of the first layers. Enabling this setting increases the adhesion of support to the build plate.

cura.support_brim_width.label: Support Inner Brim Width
cura.support_brim_width.tooltip: The width of the brim to print inside the support, on the first layer. A larger brim enhances adhesion to the build plate, at the cost of some extra material.

cura.support_brim_line_count.label: Support Inner Brim Line Count
cura.support_brim_line_count.tooltip: The number of lines used for the support inside brim. More brim lines enhance adhesion to the build plate, at the cost of some extra material.

cura.support_brim_minimum_hole_area.label: Minimum hole area in brim support
cura.support_brim_minimum_hole_area.tooltip: Holes in the support brim that have an area less than this value will be filtered out, resulting in a more consistent brim. Set to 0 to have a fully generated support brim

cura.support_base_height.label: Support Base Height
cura.support_base_height.tooltip: The height of the support base. Increasing this value will result in a sturdier support because the base will be wider. If this setting is too low, the supports will not have a sturdy base.

cura.support_inside_base_height.label: Support Inside Base Height
cura.support_inside_base_height.tooltip: The height of the inside support base. Increasing this value will result in a sturdier support because the base will be thicker. If this setting is too low, the supports will not have a sturdy base.

cura.support_outside_base_height.label: Support Outside Base Height
cura.support_outside_base_height.tooltip: The height of the outside support base. Increasing this value will result in a sturdier support because the base will be thicker. If this setting is too low, the supports will not have a sturdy base.

cura.support_base_width.label: Support Base Width
cura.support_base_width.tooltip: The width of the support base. Increasing this value will result in a sturdier support because the base will be wider. If this setting is too low, the supports will not have a sturdy base.

cura.support_base_inside_width.label: Support Base Inside Width
cura.support_base_inside_width.tooltip: The width of the inside support base. Increasing this value will result in a sturdier support. If this setting is too low, the supports will not have a sturdy inside base.

cura.support_base_outside_width.label: Support Base Outside Width
cura.support_base_outside_width.tooltip: The width of the outside support base. Increasing this value will result in a sturdier support because the base will be wider. If this setting is too low, the supports will not have a sturdy base.

cura.support_base_curve_magnitude.label: Support Base Slope
cura.support_base_curve_magnitude.tooltip: The magnitude factor used for the slope of the support base. If you increase this value, the base will become slimmer. If you decrease it, the base will become thicker.

cura.support_inside_base_curve_magnitude.label: Support Inside Base Slope
cura.support_inside_base_curve_magnitude.tooltip: The magnitude factor used for the slope of the inside support base. If you increase this value, the base will become slimmer. If you decrease it, the base will become thicker.

cura.support_outside_base_curve_magnitud.label: Support Outside Base Slope
cura.support_outside_base_curve_magnitud.tooltip: The magnitude factor used for the slope of the outside support base. If you increase this value, the base will become slimmer. If you decrease it, the base will become thicker.

cura.support_z_distance.label: Support Z Distance
cura.support_z_distance.tooltip: Distance from the top/bottom of the support structure to the print. This gap provides clearance to remove the supports after the model is printed. The topmost support layer below the model might be a fraction of regular layers.

cura.support_xy_overrides_z.label: Support Distance Priority
cura.support_xy_overrides_z.tooltip: Whether the Support X/Y Distance overrides the Support Z Distance or vice versa. When X/Y overrides Z the X/Y distance can push away the support from the model, influencing the actual Z distance to the overhang. We can disable this by not applying the X/Y distance around overhangs.

cura.support_xy_distance_overhang.label: Minimum Support X/Y Distance
cura.support_xy_distance_overhang.tooltip: Distance of the support structure from the overhang in the X/Y directions.

cura.support_bottom_stair_step_height.label: Support Stair Step Height
cura.support_bottom_stair_step_height.tooltip: The height of the steps of the stair-like bottom of support resting on the model. A low value makes the support harder to remove, but too high values can lead to unstable support structures. Set to zero to turn off the stair-like behaviour.

cura.support_bottom_stair_step_width.label: Support Stair Step Maximum Width
cura.support_bottom_stair_step_width.tooltip: The maximum width of the steps of the stair-like bottom of support resting on the model. A low value makes the support harder to remove, but too high values can lead to unstable support structures.

cura.support_bottom_stair_step_min_slope.label: Support Stair Step Minimum Slope Angle
cura.support_bottom_stair_step_min_slope.tooltip: The minimum slope of the area for stair-stepping to take effect. Low values should make support easier to remove on shallower slopes, but really low values may result in some very counter-intuitive results on other parts of the model.

cura.support_join_distance.label: Support Join Distance
cura.support_join_distance.tooltip: The maximum distance between support structures in the X/Y directions. When separate structures are closer together than this value, the structures merge into one.

cura.support_offset.label: Support Horizontal Expansion
cura.support_offset.tooltip: Amount of offset applied to all support polygons in each layer. Positive values can smooth out the support areas and result in more sturdy support.

cura.support_infill_sparse_thickness.label: Support Infill Layer Thickness
cura.support_infill_sparse_thickness.tooltip: The thickness per layer of support infill material. This value should always be a multiple of the layer height and is otherwise rounded.

cura.gradual_support_infill_steps.label: Gradual Support Infill Steps
cura.gradual_support_infill_steps.tooltip: Number of times to reduce the support infill density by half when getting further below top surfaces. Areas which are closer to top surfaces get a higher density, up to the Support Infill Density.

cura.gradual_support_infill_step_height.label: Gradual Support Infill Step Height
cura.gradual_support_infill_step_height.tooltip: The height of support infill of a given density before switching to half the density.

cura.minimum_support_area.label: Minimum Support Area
cura.minimum_support_area.tooltip: Minimum area size for support polygons. Polygons which have an area smaller than this value will not be generated.

cura.support_interface_enable.label: Enable Support Interface
cura.support_interface_enable.tooltip: Generate a dense interface between the model and the support. This will create a skin at the top of the support on which the model is printed and at the bottom of the support, where it rests on the model.

cura.support_roof_enable.label: Enable Support Roof
cura.support_roof_enable.tooltip: Generate a dense slab of material between the top of support and the model. This will create a skin between the model and support.

cura.support_bottom_enable.label: Enable Support Floor
cura.support_bottom_enable.tooltip: Generate a dense slab of material between the bottom of the support and the model. This will create a skin between the model and support.

cura.support_interface_height.label: Support Interface Thickness
cura.support_interface_height.tooltip: The thickness of the interface of the support where it touches with the model on the bottom or the top.

cura.support_roof_height.label: Support Roof Thickness
cura.support_roof_height.tooltip: The thickness of the support roofs. This controls the amount of dense layers at the top of the support on which the model rests.

cura.support_bottom_height.label: Support Floor Thickness
cura.support_bottom_height.tooltip: The thickness of the support floors. This controls the number of dense layers that are printed on top of places of a model on which support rests.

cura.support_interface_density.label: Support Interface Density
cura.support_interface_density.tooltip: Adjusts the density of the roofs and floors of the support structure. A higher value results in better overhangs, but the supports are harder to remove.

cura.support_roof_density.label: Support Roof Density
cura.support_roof_density.tooltip: The density of the roofs of the support structure. A higher value results in better overhangs, but the supports are harder to remove.

default.expr: 0 if support_roof_density == 0 else (support_roof_line_width * 100) / support_roof_density * (2 if support_roof_pattern == 'grid' else (3 if support_roof_pattern == 'triangles' else 1))

cura.support_roof_line_distance.label: Support Roof Line Distance
cura.support_roof_line_distance.tooltip: Distance between the printed support roof lines. This setting is calculated by the Support Roof Density, but can be adjusted separately.

cura.support_bottom_density.label: Support Floor Density
cura.support_bottom_density.tooltip: The density of the floors of the support structure. A higher value results in better adhesion of the support on top of the model.

default.expr: 0 if support_bottom_density == 0 else (support_bottom_line_width * 100) / support_bottom_density * (2 if support_bottom_pattern == 'grid' else (3 if support_bottom_pattern == 'triangles' else 1))

cura.support_bottom_line_distance.label: Support Floor Line Distance
cura.support_bottom_line_distance.tooltip: Distance between the printed support floor lines. This setting is calculated by the Support Floor Density, but can be adjusted separately.

cura.support_roof_pattern.label: Support Roof Pattern
cura.support_roof_pattern.tooltip: The pattern with which the roofs of the support are printed.

cura.support_bottom_pattern.label: Support Floor Pattern
cura.support_bottom_pattern.tooltip: The pattern with which the floors of the support are printed.

cura.minimum_interface_area.label: Minimum Support Interface Area
cura.minimum_interface_area.tooltip: Minimum area size for support interface polygons. Polygons which have an area smaller than this value will be printed as normal support.

cura.minimum_roof_area.label: Minimum Support Roof Area
cura.minimum_roof_area.tooltip: Minimum area size for the roofs of the support. Polygons which have an area smaller than this value will be printed as normal support.

cura.minimum_bottom_area.label: Minimum Support Floor Area
cura.minimum_bottom_area.tooltip: Minimum area size for the floors of the support. Polygons which have an area smaller than this value will be printed as normal support.

cura.support_interface_offset.label: Support Interface Horizontal Expansion
cura.support_interface_offset.tooltip: Amount of offset applied to the support interface polygons.

cura.support_roof_offset.label: Support Roof Horizontal Expansion
cura.support_roof_offset.tooltip: Amount of offset applied to the roofs of the support.

cura.support_bottom_offset.label: Support Floor Horizontal Expansion
cura.support_bottom_offset.tooltip: Amount of offset applied to the floors of the support.

cura.support_interface_priority.label: Support Interface Priority
cura.support_interface_priority.tooltip: How support interface and support will interact when they overlap. Currently only implemented for support roof.

cura.support_interface_angles.label: Support Interface Line Directions
cura.support_interface_angles.tooltip: A list of integer line directions to use. Elements from the list are used sequentially as the layers progress and when the end of the list is reached, it starts at the beginning again. The list items are separated by commas and the whole list is contained in square brackets. Default is an empty list which means use the default angles (alternates between 45 and 135 degrees if interfaces are quite thick or 90 degrees).

cura.support_roof_angles.label: Support Roof Line Directions
cura.support_roof_angles.tooltip: A list of integer line directions to use. Elements from the list are used sequentially as the layers progress and when the end of the list is reached, it starts at the beginning again. The list items are separated by commas and the whole list is contained in square brackets. Default is an empty list which means use the default angles (alternates between 45 and 135 degrees if interfaces are quite thick or 90 degrees).

cura.support_bottom_angles.label: Support Floor Line Directions
cura.support_bottom_angles.tooltip: A list of integer line directions to use. Elements from the list are used sequentially as the layers progress and when the end of the list is reached, it starts at the beginning again. The list items are separated by commas and the whole list is contained in square brackets. Default is an empty list which means use the default angles (alternates between 45 and 135 degrees if interfaces are quite thick or 90 degrees).

cura.support_fan_enable.label: Fan Speed Override
cura.support_fan_enable.tooltip: When enabled, the print cooling fan speed is altered for the skin regions immediately above the support.

cura.support_supported_skin_fan_speed.label: Supported Skin Fan Speed
cura.support_supported_skin_fan_speed.tooltip: Percentage fan speed to use when printing the skin regions immediately above the support. Using a high fan speed can make the support easier to remove.

cura.support_use_towers.label: Use Towers
cura.support_use_towers.tooltip: Use specialized towers to support tiny overhang areas. These towers have a larger diameter than the region they support. Near the overhang the towers' diameter decreases, forming a roof.

cura.support_tower_diameter.label: Tower Diameter
cura.support_tower_diameter.tooltip: The diameter of a special tower.

cura.support_tower_maximum_supported_dia.label: Maximum Tower-Supported Diameter
cura.support_tower_maximum_supported_dia.tooltip: Maximum diameter in the X/Y directions of a small area which is to be supported by a specialized support tower.

cura.support_tower_roof_angle.label: Tower Roof Angle
cura.support_tower_roof_angle.tooltip: The angle of a rooftop of a tower. A higher value results in pointed tower roofs, a lower value results in flattened tower roofs.

cura.support_mesh_drop_down.label: Drop Down Support Mesh
cura.support_mesh_drop_down.tooltip: Make support everywhere below the support mesh, so that there's no overhang in the support mesh.

cura.support_meshes_present.label: Scene Has Support Meshes
cura.support_meshes_present.tooltip: There are support meshes present in the scene. This setting is controlled by Cura.

cura.support_paint_resolution.label: Support Painting Precision
cura.support_paint_resolution.tooltip: The precision of the details when generating support based on painting data. A lower precision will provide more details, but increase the slicing time and memory.

cura.prime_blob_enable.label: Enable Prime Blob
cura.prime_blob_enable.tooltip: Whether to prime the filament with a blob before printing. Turning this setting on will ensure that the extruder will have material ready at the nozzle before printing. Printing Brim or Skirt can act like priming too, in which case turning this setting off saves some time.

cura.extruder_prime_pos_x.label: Extruder Prime X Position
cura.extruder_prime_pos_x.tooltip: The X coordinate of the position where the nozzle primes at the start of printing.

cura.extruder_prime_pos_y.label: Extruder Prime Y Position
cura.extruder_prime_pos_y.tooltip: The Y coordinate of the position where the nozzle primes at the start of printing.

cura.adhesion_type.label: Build Plate Adhesion Type
cura.adhesion_type.tooltip: Different options that help to improve both priming your extrusion and adhesion to the build plate. Brim adds a single layer flat area around the base of your model to prevent warping. Raft adds a thick grid with a roof below the model. Skirt is a line printed around the model, but not connected to the model.

cura.adhesion_extruder_nr.label: Build Plate Adhesion Extruder
cura.adhesion_extruder_nr.tooltip: The extruder train to use for printing the skirt/brim/raft. This is used in multi-extrusion.

cura.skirt_brim_extruder_nr.label: Skirt/Brim Extruder
cura.skirt_brim_extruder_nr.tooltip: The extruder train to use for printing the skirt or brim. This is used in multi-extrusion.

cura.raft_base_extruder_nr.label: Raft Base Extruder
cura.raft_base_extruder_nr.tooltip: The extruder train to use for printing the first layer of the raft. This is used in multi-extrusion.

cura.raft_interface_extruder_nr.label: Raft Middle Extruder
cura.raft_interface_extruder_nr.tooltip: The extruder train to use for printing the middle layer of the raft. This is used in multi-extrusion.

cura.raft_surface_extruder_nr.label: Raft Top Extruder
cura.raft_surface_extruder_nr.tooltip: The extruder train to use for printing the top layer(s) of the raft. This is used in multi-extrusion.

cura.skirt_brim_minimal_length.label: Skirt/Brim Minimum Length
cura.skirt_brim_minimal_length.tooltip: The minimum length of the skirt or brim. If this length is not reached by all skirt or brim lines together, more skirt or brim lines will be added until the minimum length is reached. Note: If the line count is set to 0 this is ignored.

cura.brim_line_count.label: Brim Line Count
cura.brim_line_count.tooltip: The number of lines used for a brim. More brim lines enhance adhesion to the build plate, but also reduces the effective print area.

cura.brim_replaces_support.label: Brim Replaces Support
cura.brim_replaces_support.tooltip: Enforce brim to be printed around the model even if that space would otherwise be occupied by support. This replaces some regions of the first layer of support by brim regions.

cura.brim_location.label: Brim Location
cura.brim_location.tooltip: Print a brim on the outside of the model, inside, or both. Depending on the model, this helps reducing the amount of brim you need to remove afterwards, while ensuring a proper bed adhesion.

cura.brim_inside_margin.label: Brim Avoid Margin
cura.brim_inside_margin.tooltip: A brim around a model may touch an other model where you don't want it. This removes all brim within this distance from brimless models.

cura.brim_smart_ordering.label: Smart Brim
cura.brim_smart_ordering.tooltip: Swap print order of the innermost and second innermost brim lines. This improves brim removal.

cura.raft_margin.label: Raft Extra Margin
cura.raft_margin.tooltip: If the raft is enabled, this is the extra raft area around the model which is also given a raft. Increasing this margin will create a stronger raft while using more material and leaving less area for your print.

cura.raft_base_margin.label: Raft Base Extra Margin
cura.raft_base_margin.tooltip: If the raft base is enabled, this is the extra raft area around the model which is also given a raft. Increasing this margin will create a stronger raft while using more material and leaving less area for your print.

cura.raft_interface_margin.label: Raft Middle Extra Margin
cura.raft_interface_margin.tooltip: If the raft middle is enabled, this is the extra raft area around the model which is also given a raft. Increasing this margin will create a stronger raft while using more material and leaving less area for your print.

cura.raft_surface_margin.label: Raft Top Extra Margin
cura.raft_surface_margin.tooltip: If the raft top is enabled, this is the extra raft area around the model which is also given a raft. Increasing this margin will create a stronger raft while using more material and leaving less area for your print.

cura.raft_remove_inside_corners.label: Remove Raft Inside Corners
cura.raft_remove_inside_corners.tooltip: Remove inside corners from the raft, causing the raft to become convex.

cura.raft_base_remove_inside_corners.label: Remove Raft Base Inside Corners
cura.raft_base_remove_inside_corners.tooltip: Remove inside corners from the raft base, causing the raft to become convex.

cura.raft_interface_remove_inside_corner.label: Remove Raft Middle Inside Corners
cura.raft_interface_remove_inside_corner.tooltip: Remove inside corners from the raft middle part, causing the raft to become convex.

cura.raft_surface_remove_inside_corners.label: Remove Raft Top Inside Corners
cura.raft_surface_remove_inside_corners.tooltip: Remove inside corners from the raft top part, causing the raft to become convex.

cura.raft_smoothing.label: Raft Smoothing
cura.raft_smoothing.tooltip: This setting controls how much inner corners in the raft outline are rounded. Inward corners are rounded to a semi circle with a radius equal to the value given here. This setting also removes holes in the raft outline which are smaller than such a circle.

cura.raft_base_smoothing.label: Raft Base Smoothing
cura.raft_base_smoothing.tooltip: This setting controls how much inner corners in the raft base outline are rounded. Inward corners are rounded to a semi circle with a radius equal to the value given here. This setting also removes holes in the raft outline which are smaller than such a circle.

cura.raft_interface_smoothing.label: Raft Middle Smoothing
cura.raft_interface_smoothing.tooltip: This setting controls how much inner corners in the raft middle outline are rounded. Inward corners are rounded to a semi circle with a radius equal to the value given here. This setting also removes holes in the raft outline which are smaller than such a circle.

cura.raft_surface_smoothing.label: Raft Top Smoothing
cura.raft_surface_smoothing.tooltip: This setting controls how much inner corners in the raft top outline are rounded. Inward corners are rounded to a semi circle with a radius equal to the value given here. This setting also removes holes in the raft outline which are smaller than such a circle.

cura.layer_0_z_overlap.label: Initial Layer Z Overlap
cura.layer_0_z_overlap.tooltip:
Make the first and second layer of the model overlap in the Z direction to compensate for the filament lost in the airgap. All models above the first model layer will be shifted down by this amount.
It may be noted that sometimes the second layer is printed below initial layer because of this setting. This is intended behavior

cura.raft_base_thickness.label: Raft Base Thickness
cura.raft_base_thickness.tooltip: Layer thickness of the base raft layer. This should be a thick layer which sticks firmly to the printer build plate.

cura.raft_base_line_width.label: Raft Base Line Width
cura.raft_base_line_width.tooltip: Width of the lines in the base raft layer. These should be thick lines to assist in build plate adhesion.

cura.raft_base_line_spacing.label: Raft Base Line Spacing
cura.raft_base_line_spacing.tooltip: The distance between the raft lines for the base raft layer. Wide spacing makes for easy removal of the raft from the build plate.

cura.raft_base_infill_overlap.label: Raft Base Infill Overlap Percentage
cura.raft_base_infill_overlap.tooltip: The amount of overlap between the infill and the walls of the raft base, as a percentage of the infill line width. A slight overlap allows the walls to connect firmly to the infill.

cura.raft_base_infill_overlap_mm.label: Raft Base Infill Overlap
cura.raft_base_infill_overlap_mm.tooltip: The amount of overlap between the infill and the walls of the raft base. A slight overlap allows the walls to connect firmly to the infill.

cura.raft_interface_layers.label: Raft Middle Layers
cura.raft_interface_layers.tooltip: The number of layers between the base and the surface of the raft. These comprise the main thickness of the raft. Increasing this creates a thicker, sturdier raft.

cura.raft_interface_thickness.label: Raft Middle Thickness
cura.raft_interface_thickness.tooltip: Layer thickness of the middle raft layer.

cura.raft_interface_line_width.label: Raft Middle Line Width
cura.raft_interface_line_width.tooltip: Width of the lines in the middle raft layer. Making the second layer extrude more causes the lines to stick to the build plate.

cura.raft_interface_line_spacing.label: Raft Middle Spacing
cura.raft_interface_line_spacing.tooltip: The distance between the raft lines for the middle raft layer. The spacing of the middle should be quite wide, while being dense enough to support the top raft layers.

cura.raft_interface_z_offset.label: Raft Interface Z Offset
cura.raft_interface_z_offset.tooltip: When printing the first layer of the raft interface, translate by this offset to customize the adhesion between base and interface. A negative offset should improve the adhesion.

cura.raft_interface_infill_overlap.label: Raft Interface Infill Overlap Percentage
cura.raft_interface_infill_overlap.tooltip: The amount of overlap between the infill and the walls of the raft interface, as a percentage of the infill line width. A slight overlap allows the walls to connect firmly to the infill.

cura.raft_interface_infill_overlap_mm.label: Raft Interface Infill Overlap
cura.raft_interface_infill_overlap_mm.tooltip: The amount of overlap between the infill and the walls of the raft interface. A slight overlap allows the walls to connect firmly to the infill.

cura.raft_surface_thickness.label: Raft Top Layer Thickness
cura.raft_surface_thickness.tooltip: Layer thickness of the top raft layers.

cura.raft_surface_line_width.label: Raft Top Line Width
cura.raft_surface_line_width.tooltip: Width of the lines in the top surface of the raft. These can be thin lines so that the top of the raft becomes smooth.

cura.raft_surface_line_spacing.label: Raft Top Spacing
cura.raft_surface_line_spacing.tooltip: The distance between the raft lines for the top raft layers. The spacing should be equal to the line width, so that the surface is solid.

cura.raft_surface_z_offset.label: Raft Surface Z Offset
cura.raft_surface_z_offset.tooltip: When printing the first layer of the raft surface, translate by this offset to customize the adhesion between interface and surface. A negative offset should improve the adhesion.

cura.raft_surface_monotonic.label: Monotonic Raft Top Surface Order
cura.raft_surface_monotonic.tooltip: Print raft top surface lines in an ordering that causes them to always overlap with adjacent lines in a single direction. This takes slightly more time to print, but makes the surface look more consistent, which is also visible on the model bottom surface.

cura.raft_surface_infill_overlap.label: Raft Surface Infill Overlap Percentage
cura.raft_surface_infill_overlap.tooltip: The amount of overlap between the infill and the walls of the raft surface, as a percentage of the infill line width. A slight overlap allows the walls to connect firmly to the infill.

cura.raft_surface_infill_overlap_mm.label: Raft Surface Infill Overlap
cura.raft_surface_infill_overlap_mm.tooltip: The amount of overlap between the infill and the walls of the raft surface. A slight overlap allows the walls to connect firmly to the infill.

cura.raft_wall_count.label: Raft Wall Count
cura.raft_wall_count.tooltip: The number of contours to print around the linear pattern of the raft.

cura.raft_base_wall_count.label: Raft Base Wall Count
cura.raft_base_wall_count.tooltip: The number of contours to print around the linear pattern in the base layer of the raft.

cura.raft_interface_wall_count.label: Raft Middle Wall Count
cura.raft_interface_wall_count.tooltip: The number of contours to print around the linear pattern in the middle layers of the raft.

cura.raft_surface_wall_count.label: Raft Top Wall Count
cura.raft_surface_wall_count.tooltip: The number of contours to print around the linear pattern in the top layers of the raft.

cura.raft_speed.label: Raft Print Speed
cura.raft_speed.tooltip: The speed at which the raft is printed.

cura.raft_base_speed.label: Raft Base Print Speed
cura.raft_base_speed.tooltip: The speed at which the base raft layer is printed. This should be printed quite slowly, as the volume of material coming out of the nozzle is quite high.

cura.raft_interface_speed.label: Raft Middle Print Speed
cura.raft_interface_speed.tooltip: The speed at which the middle raft layer is printed. This should be printed quite slowly, as the volume of material coming out of the nozzle is quite high.

cura.raft_surface_speed.label: Raft Top Print Speed
cura.raft_surface_speed.tooltip: The speed at which the top raft layers are printed. These should be printed a bit slower, so that the nozzle can slowly smooth out adjacent surface lines.

cura.raft_acceleration.label: Raft Print Acceleration
cura.raft_acceleration.tooltip: The acceleration with which the raft is printed.

cura.raft_base_acceleration.label: Raft Base Print Acceleration
cura.raft_base_acceleration.tooltip: The acceleration with which the base raft layer is printed.

cura.raft_interface_acceleration.label: Raft Middle Print Acceleration
cura.raft_interface_acceleration.tooltip: The acceleration with which the middle raft layer is printed.

cura.raft_surface_acceleration.label: Raft Top Print Acceleration
cura.raft_surface_acceleration.tooltip: The acceleration with which the top raft layers are printed.

cura.raft_jerk.label: Raft Print Jerk
cura.raft_jerk.tooltip: The jerk with which the raft is printed.

cura.raft_base_jerk.label: Raft Base Print Jerk
cura.raft_base_jerk.tooltip: The jerk with which the base raft layer is printed.

cura.raft_interface_jerk.label: Raft Middle Print Jerk
cura.raft_interface_jerk.tooltip: The jerk with which the middle raft layer is printed.

cura.raft_surface_jerk.label: Raft Top Print Jerk
cura.raft_surface_jerk.tooltip: The jerk with which the top raft layers are printed.

cura.raft_fan_speed.label: Raft Fan Speed
cura.raft_fan_speed.tooltip: The fan speed for the raft.

cura.raft_base_fan_speed.label: Raft Base Fan Speed
cura.raft_base_fan_speed.tooltip: The fan speed for the base raft layer.

cura.raft_interface_fan_speed.label: Raft Middle Fan Speed
cura.raft_interface_fan_speed.tooltip: The fan speed for the middle raft layer.

cura.raft_surface_fan_speed.label: Raft Top Fan Speed
cura.raft_surface_fan_speed.tooltip: The fan speed for the top raft layers.

cura.raft_flow.label: Raft Flow
cura.raft_flow.tooltip: The amount of material, relative to a normal extrusion line, to extrude during raft printing. Having an increased flow may improve adhesion and raft structural strength.

cura.raft_base_flow.label: Raft Base Flow
cura.raft_base_flow.tooltip: The amount of material, relative to a normal extrusion line, to extrude during raft base printing. Having an increased flow may improve adhesion and raft structural strength.

cura.raft_interface_flow.label: Raft Interface Flow
cura.raft_interface_flow.tooltip: The amount of material, relative to a normal extrusion line, to extrude during raft interface printing. Having an increased flow may improve adhesion and raft structural strength.

cura.raft_surface_flow.label: Raft Surface Flow
cura.raft_surface_flow.tooltip: The amount of material, relative to a normal extrusion line, to extrude during raft surface printing. Having an increased flow may improve adhesion and raft structural strength.

cura.machine_scan_first_layer.label: Scan the first layer
cura.machine_scan_first_layer.tooltip: Whether to scan the first layer for layer adhesion problems.

cura.prime_tower_mode.label: Prime Tower Type
cura.prime_tower_mode.tooltip:
How to generate the prime tower:
  • Normal: create a bucket in which secondary materials are primed
  • Interleaved: create a prime tower as sparse as possible. This will save time and filament, but is only possible if the used materials adhere to each other

cura.prime_tower_min_volume.label: Prime Tower Minimum Volume
cura.prime_tower_min_volume.tooltip: The minimum volume for each layer of the prime tower in order to purge enough material.

cura.prime_tower_max_bridging_distance.label: Prime Tower Maximum Bridging Distance
cura.prime_tower_max_bridging_distance.tooltip: The maximum length of the branches which may be printed over the air.

cura.prime_tower_min_shell_thickness.label: Prime Tower Minimum Shell Thickness
cura.prime_tower_min_shell_thickness.tooltip: The minimum thickness of the prime tower shell. You may increase it to make the prime tower stronger.

cura.prime_tower_wipe_enabled.label: Wipe Inactive Nozzle on Prime Tower
cura.prime_tower_wipe_enabled.tooltip: After printing the prime tower with one nozzle, wipe the oozed material from the other nozzle off on the prime tower.

cura.prime_tower_brim_enable.label: Prime Tower Base
cura.prime_tower_brim_enable.tooltip: By enabling this setting, your prime-tower will get a brim, even if the model doesn't. If you want a sturdier base for a high tower, you can increase the base height.

cura.prime_tower_base_size.label: Prime Tower Base Size
cura.prime_tower_base_size.tooltip: The width of the prime tower brim/base. A larger base enhances adhesion to the build plate, but also reduces the effective print area.

cura.prime_tower_base_height.label: Prime Tower Base Height
cura.prime_tower_base_height.tooltip: The height of the prime tower base. Increasing this value will result in a more sturdy prime tower because the base will be wider. If this setting is too low, the prime tower will not have a sturdy base.

cura.prime_tower_base_curve_magnitude.label: Prime Tower Base Slope
cura.prime_tower_base_curve_magnitude.tooltip: The magnitude factor used for the slope of the prime tower base. If you increase this value, the base will become slimmer. If you decrease it, the base will become thicker.

cura.prime_tower_raft_base_line_spacing.label: Prime Tower Raft Line Spacing
cura.prime_tower_raft_base_line_spacing.tooltip: The distance between the raft lines for the unique prime tower raft layer. Wide spacing makes for easy removal of the raft from the build plate.

cura.ooze_shield_enabled.label: Enable Ooze Shield
cura.ooze_shield_enabled.tooltip: Enable exterior ooze shield. This will create a shell around the model which is likely to wipe a second nozzle if it's at the same height as the first nozzle.

cura.ooze_shield_angle.label: Ooze Shield Angle
cura.ooze_shield_angle.tooltip: The maximum angle a part in the ooze shield will have. With 0 degrees being vertical, and 90 degrees being horizontal. A smaller angle leads to less failed ooze shields, but more material.

cura.ooze_shield_dist.label: Ooze Shield Distance
cura.ooze_shield_dist.tooltip: Distance of the ooze shield from the print, in the X/Y directions.

cura.switch_extruder_retraction_amount.label: Nozzle Switch Retraction Distance
cura.switch_extruder_retraction_amount.tooltip: The amount of retraction when switching extruders. Set to 0 for no retraction at all. This should generally be the same as the length of the heat zone.

cura.switch_extruder_retraction_speeds.label: Nozzle Switch Retraction Speed
cura.switch_extruder_retraction_speeds.tooltip: The speed at which the filament is retracted. A higher retraction speed works better, but a very high retraction speed can lead to filament grinding.

cura.switch_extruder_retraction_speed.label: Nozzle Switch Retract Speed
cura.switch_extruder_retraction_speed.tooltip: The speed at which the filament is retracted during a nozzle switch retract.

cura.switch_extruder_prime_speed.label: Nozzle Switch Prime Speed
cura.switch_extruder_prime_speed.tooltip: The speed at which the filament is pushed back after a nozzle switch retraction.

cura.switch_extruder_extra_prime_amount.label: Nozzle Switch Extra Prime Amount
cura.switch_extruder_extra_prime_amount.tooltip: Extra material to prime after nozzle switching.

cura.interlocking_enable.label: Generate Interlocking Structure
cura.interlocking_enable.tooltip: At the locations where models touch, generate an interlocking beam structure. This improves the adhesion between models, especially models printed in different materials.

cura.multi_material_paint_resolution.label: Multi-material Precision
cura.multi_material_paint_resolution.tooltip: The precision of the details when generating multi-material shapes based on painting data. A lower precision will provide more details, but increase the slicing time and memory.

cura.multi_material_paint_depth.label: Multi-material Depth
cura.multi_material_paint_depth.tooltip: The depth of the painted details inside the model. A higher depth will provide a better interlocking, but increase slicing time and memory. Set a very high value to go as deep as possible. The actually calculated depth may vary.

cura.meshfix_union_all.label: Union Overlapping Volumes
cura.meshfix_union_all.tooltip: Ignore the internal geometry arising from overlapping volumes within a mesh and print the volumes as one. This may cause unintended internal cavities to disappear.

cura.meshfix_union_all_remove_holes.label: Remove All Holes
cura.meshfix_union_all_remove_holes.tooltip: Remove the holes in each layer and keep only the outside shape. This will ignore any invisible internal geometry. However, it also ignores layer holes which can be viewed from above or below.

cura.meshfix_extensive_stitching.label: Extensive Stitching
cura.meshfix_extensive_stitching.tooltip: Extensive stitching tries to stitch up open holes in the mesh by closing the hole with touching polygons. This option can introduce a lot of processing time.

cura.meshfix_keep_open_polygons.label: Keep Disconnected Faces
cura.meshfix_keep_open_polygons.tooltip: Normally Cura tries to stitch up small holes in the mesh and remove parts of a layer with big holes. Enabling this option keeps those parts which cannot be stitched. This option should be used as a last resort option when everything else fails to produce proper g-code.

cura.multiple_mesh_overlap.label: Merged Meshes Overlap
cura.multiple_mesh_overlap.tooltip: Make meshes which are touching each other overlap a bit. This makes them bond together better.

cura.carve_multiple_volumes.label: Remove Mesh Intersection
cura.carve_multiple_volumes.tooltip: Remove areas where multiple meshes are overlapping with each other. This may be used if merged dual material objects overlap with each other.

cura.alternate_carve_order.label: Alternate Mesh Removal
cura.alternate_carve_order.tooltip: Switch to which mesh intersecting volumes will belong with every layer, so that the overlapping meshes become interwoven. Turning this setting off will cause one of the meshes to obtain all of the volume in the overlap, while it is removed from the other meshes.

cura.remove_empty_first_layers.label: Remove Empty First Layers
cura.remove_empty_first_layers.tooltip: Remove empty layers beneath the first printed layer if they are present. Disabling this setting can cause empty first layers if the Slicing Tolerance setting is set to Exclusive or Middle. It will be ignored if support is present.

cura.meshfix_maximum_travel_resolution.label: Maximum Travel Resolution
cura.meshfix_maximum_travel_resolution.tooltip: The minimum size of a travel line segment after slicing. If you increase this, the travel moves will have less smooth corners. This may allow the printer to keep up with the speed it has to process g-code, but it may cause model avoidance to become less accurate.

cura.meshfix_maximum_deviation.label: Maximum Deviation
cura.meshfix_maximum_deviation.tooltip: The maximum deviation allowed when reducing the resolution for the Maximum Resolution setting. If you increase this, the print will be less accurate, but the g-code will be smaller. Maximum Deviation is a limit for Maximum Resolution, so if the two conflict the Maximum Deviation will always be held true.

cura.meshfix_maximum_extrusion_area_devi.label: Maximum Extrusion Area Deviation
cura.meshfix_maximum_extrusion_area_devi.tooltip: The maximum extrusion area deviation allowed when removing intermediate points from a straight line. An intermediate point may serve as width-changing point in a long straight line. Therefore, if it is removed, it will cause the line to have a uniform width and, as a result, lose (or gain) a bit of extrusion area. If you increase this you may notice slight under- (or over-) extrusion in between straight parallel walls, as more intermediate width-changing points will be allowed to be removed. Your print will be less accurate, but the g-code will be smaller.

cura.meshfix_fluid_motion_enabled.label: Enable Fluid Motion
cura.meshfix_fluid_motion_enabled.tooltip: When enabled tool paths are corrected for printers with smooth motion planners. Small movements that deviate from the general tool path direction are smoothed to improve fluid motions.

cura.meshfix_fluid_motion_shift_distance.label: Fluid Motion Shift Distance
cura.meshfix_fluid_motion_shift_distance.tooltip: Distance points are shifted to smooth the path

cura.meshfix_fluid_motion_small_distance.label: Fluid Motion Small Distance
cura.meshfix_fluid_motion_small_distance.tooltip: Distance points are shifted to smooth the path

cura.meshfix_fluid_motion_angle.label: Fluid Motion Angle
cura.meshfix_fluid_motion_angle.tooltip: If a toolpath-segment deviates more than this angle from the general motion it is smoothed.

cura.user_defined_print_order_enabled.label: Set Print Sequence Manually
cura.user_defined_print_order_enabled.tooltip: Allows you to order the object list to manually set the print sequence. First object from the list will be printed first.

cura.infill_mesh.label: Infill Mesh
cura.infill_mesh.tooltip: Use this mesh to modify the infill of other meshes with which it overlaps. Replaces infill regions of other meshes with regions for this mesh. It's suggested to only print one Wall and no Top/Bottom Skin for this mesh.

cura.infill_mesh_order.label: Mesh Processing Rank
cura.infill_mesh_order.tooltip: Determines the priority of this mesh when considering multiple overlapping infill meshes. Areas where multiple infill meshes overlap will take on the settings of the mesh with the highest rank. An infill mesh with a higher rank will modify the infill of infill meshes with lower rank and normal meshes.

cura.cutting_mesh.label: Cutting Mesh
cura.cutting_mesh.tooltip: Limit the volume of this mesh to within other meshes. You can use this to make certain areas of one mesh print with different settings and with a whole different extruder.

cura.mold_enabled.label: Mold
cura.mold_enabled.tooltip: Print models as a mold, which can be cast in order to get a model which resembles the models on the build plate.

cura.mold_width.label: Minimal Mold Width
cura.mold_width.tooltip: The minimal distance between the outside of the mold and the outside of the model.

cura.mold_roof_height.label: Mold Roof Height
cura.mold_roof_height.tooltip: The height above horizontal parts in your model which to print mold.

cura.mold_angle.label: Mold Angle
cura.mold_angle.tooltip: The angle of overhang of the outer walls created for the mold. 0° will make the outer shell of the mold vertical, while 90° will make the outside of the model follow the contour of the model.

cura.support_mesh.label: Support Mesh
cura.support_mesh.tooltip: Use this mesh to specify support areas. This can be used to generate support structure.

cura.anti_overhang_mesh.label: Anti Overhang Mesh
cura.anti_overhang_mesh.tooltip: Use this mesh to specify where no part of the model should be detected as overhang. This can be used to remove unwanted support structure.

cura.magic_mesh_surface_mode.label: Surface Mode
cura.magic_mesh_surface_mode.tooltip: Treat the model as a surface only, a volume, or volumes with loose surfaces. The normal print mode only prints enclosed volumes. "Surface" prints a single wall tracing the mesh surface with no infill and no top/bottom skin. "Both" prints enclosed volumes like normal and any remaining polygons as surfaces.

cura.slicing_tolerance.label: Slicing Tolerance
cura.slicing_tolerance.tooltip: Vertical tolerance in the sliced layers. The contours of a layer are normally generated by taking cross sections through the middle of each layer's thickness (Middle). Alternatively each layer can have the areas which fall inside of the volume throughout the entire thickness of the layer (Exclusive) or a layer has the areas which fall inside anywhere within the layer (Inclusive). Inclusive retains the most details, Exclusive makes for the best fit and Middle stays closest to the original surface.

cura.infill_enable_travel_optimization.label: Infill Travel Optimization
cura.infill_enable_travel_optimization.tooltip: When enabled, the order in which the infill lines are printed is optimized to reduce the distance travelled. The reduction in travel time achieved very much depends on the model being sliced, infill pattern, density, etc. Note that, for some models that have many small areas of infill, the time to slice the model may be greatly increased.

cura.material_flow_temp_graph.label: Flow Temperature Graph
cura.material_flow_temp_graph.tooltip: Data linking material flow (in mm3 per second) to temperature (degrees Celsius).

cura.minimum_polygon_circumference.label: Minimum Polygon Circumference
cura.minimum_polygon_circumference.tooltip: Polygons in sliced layers that have a circumference smaller than this amount will be filtered out. Lower values lead to higher resolution mesh at the cost of slicing time. It is meant mostly for high resolution SLA printers and very tiny 3D models with a lot of details.

cura.support_skip_some_zags.label: Break Up Support In Chunks
cura.support_skip_some_zags.tooltip: Skip some support line connections to make the support structure easier to break away. This setting is applicable to the Zig Zag support infill pattern.

cura.support_skip_zag_per_mm.label: Support Chunk Size
cura.support_skip_zag_per_mm.tooltip: Leave out a connection between support lines once every N millimeter to make the support structure easier to break away.

cura.support_zag_skip_count.label: Support Chunk Line Count
cura.support_zag_skip_count.tooltip: Skip one in every N connection lines to make the support structure easier to break away.

cura.draft_shield_enabled.label: Enable Draft Shield
cura.draft_shield_enabled.tooltip: This will create a wall around the model, which traps (hot) air and shields against exterior airflow. Especially useful for materials which warp easily.

cura.draft_shield_dist.label: Draft Shield X/Y Distance
cura.draft_shield_dist.tooltip: Distance of the draft shield from the print, in the X/Y directions.

cura.draft_shield_height_limitation.label: Draft Shield Limitation
cura.draft_shield_height_limitation.tooltip: Set the height of the draft shield. Choose to print the draft shield at the full height of the model or at a limited height.

cura.draft_shield_height.label: Draft Shield Height
cura.draft_shield_height.tooltip: Height limitation of the draft shield. Above this height no draft shield will be printed.

cura.conical_overhang_enabled.label: Make Overhang Printable
cura.conical_overhang_enabled.tooltip: Change the geometry of the printed model such that minimal support is required. Steep overhangs will become shallow overhangs. Overhanging areas will drop down to become more vertical.

cura.conical_overhang_angle.label: Maximum Model Angle
cura.conical_overhang_angle.tooltip: The maximum angle of overhangs after the they have been made printable. At a value of 0° all overhangs are replaced by a piece of model connected to the build plate, 90° will not change the model in any way.

cura.conical_overhang_hole_size.label: Maximum Overhang Hole Area
cura.conical_overhang_hole_size.tooltip: The maximum area of a hole in the base of the model before it's removed by Make Overhang Printable.  Holes smaller than this will be retained.  A value of 0 mm² will fill all holes in the models base.

cura.coasting_enable.label: Enable Coasting
cura.coasting_enable.tooltip: Coasting replaces the last part of an extrusion path with a travel path. The oozed material is used to print the last piece of the extrusion path in order to reduce stringing.

cura.coasting_volume.label: Coasting Volume
cura.coasting_volume.tooltip: The volume otherwise oozed. This value should generally be close to the nozzle diameter cubed.

cura.coasting_min_volume.label: Minimum Volume Before Coasting
cura.coasting_min_volume.tooltip: The smallest volume an extrusion path should have before allowing coasting. For smaller extrusion paths, less pressure has been built up in the bowden tube and so the coasted volume is scaled linearly. This value should always be larger than the Coasting Volume.

cura.coasting_speed.label: Coasting Speed
cura.coasting_speed.tooltip: The speed by which to move during coasting, relative to the speed of the extrusion path. A value slightly under 100% is advised, since during the coasting move the pressure in the bowden tube drops.

cura.cross_infill_pocket_size.label: Cross 3D Pocket Size
cura.cross_infill_pocket_size.tooltip: The size of pockets at four-way crossings in the cross 3D pattern at heights where the pattern is touching itself.

cura.cross_infill_density_image.label: Cross Infill Density Image
cura.cross_infill_density_image.tooltip: The file location of an image of which the brightness values determine the minimal density at the corresponding location in the infill of the print.

cura.cross_support_density_image.label: Cross Fill Density Image for Support
cura.cross_support_density_image.tooltip: The file location of an image of which the brightness values determine the minimal density at the corresponding location in the support.

cura.support_conical_enabled.label: Enable Conical Support
cura.support_conical_enabled.tooltip: Make support areas smaller at the bottom than at the overhang.

cura.support_conical_angle.label: Conical Support Angle
cura.support_conical_angle.tooltip: The angle of the tilt of conical support. With 0 degrees being vertical, and 90 degrees being horizontal. Smaller angles cause the support to be more sturdy, but consist of more material. Negative angles cause the base of the support to be wider than the top.

cura.support_conical_min_width.label: Conical Support Minimum Width
cura.support_conical_min_width.tooltip: Minimum width to which the base of the conical support area is reduced. Small widths can lead to unstable support structures.

cura.magic_fuzzy_skin_outside_only.label: Fuzzy Skin Outside Only
cura.magic_fuzzy_skin_outside_only.tooltip: Jitter only the parts' outlines and not the parts' holes.

cura.magic_fuzzy_skin_point_density.label: Fuzzy Skin Density
cura.magic_fuzzy_skin_point_density.tooltip: The average density of points introduced on each polygon in a layer. Note that the original points of the polygon are discarded, so a low density results in a reduction of the resolution.

cura.flow_rate_max_extrusion_offset.label: Flow Rate Compensation Max Extrusion Offset
cura.flow_rate_max_extrusion_offset.tooltip: The maximum distance in mm to move the filament to compensate for changes in flow rate.

cura.flow_rate_extrusion_offset_factor.label: Flow Rate Compensation Factor
cura.flow_rate_extrusion_offset_factor.tooltip: How far to move the filament in order to compensate for changes in flow rate, as a percentage of how far the filament would move in one second of extrusion.

cura.adaptive_layer_height_enabled.label: Use Adaptive Layers
cura.adaptive_layer_height_enabled.tooltip: Adaptive layers computes the layer heights depending on the shape of the model.

cura.adaptive_layer_height_variation.label: Adaptive Layers Maximum Variation
cura.adaptive_layer_height_variation.tooltip: The maximum allowed height different from the base layer height.

cura.adaptive_layer_height_variation_ste.label: Adaptive Layers Variation Step Size
cura.adaptive_layer_height_variation_ste.tooltip: The difference in height of the next layer height compared to the previous one.

cura.adaptive_layer_height_threshold.label: Adaptive Layers Topography Size
cura.adaptive_layer_height_threshold.tooltip: Target horizontal distance between two adjacent layers. Reducing this setting causes thinner layers to be used to bring the edges of the layers closer together.

cura.wall_overhang_angle.label: Overhanging Wall Angle
cura.wall_overhang_angle.tooltip: Walls that overhang more than this angle will be printed using overhanging wall settings. When the value is 90, no walls will be treated as overhanging. Overhang that gets supported by support will not be treated as overhang either. Furthermore, any line that's less than half overhanging will also not be treated as overhang.

cura.cool_min_layer_time_overhang.label: Minimum Layer Time with Overhang
cura.cool_min_layer_time_overhang.tooltip: The minimum time spent in a layer that contains overhanging extrusions. This forces the printer to slow down, to at least spend the time set here in one layer. This allows the printed material to cool down properly before printing the next layer. Layers may still take shorter than the minimal layer time if Lift Head is disabled and if the Minimum Speed would otherwise be violated.

cura.cool_min_layer_time_overhang_min_se.label: Minimum Overhang Segment Length
cura.cool_min_layer_time_overhang_min_se.tooltip: When trying to apply the minimum layer time specific for overhanging layers, it will be applied only if at least one consecutive overhanging extrusion move is longer than this value.

cura.seam_overhang_angle.label: Seam Overhanging Wall Angle
cura.seam_overhang_angle.tooltip: Try to prevent seams on walls that overhang more than this angle. When the value is 90, no walls will be treated as overhanging.

cura.wall_overhang_speed_factors.label: Overhanging Wall Speeds
cura.wall_overhang_speed_factors.tooltip: Overhanging walls will be printed at a percentage of their normal print speed. You can specify multiple values, so that even more overhanging walls will be printed even slower, e.g. by setting [75, 50, 25]

cura.bridge_settings_enabled.label: Enable Bridge Settings
cura.bridge_settings_enabled.tooltip: Detect bridges and modify print speed, flow and fan settings while bridges are printed.

cura.bridge_wall_max_deviation.label: Maximum Bridge Deviation
cura.bridge_wall_max_deviation.tooltip: Bridge-walls shouldn't deviate from straight lines more than this, anything that falls outside of the area of maximum allowed deviation (defined by the aligned bounding box around the anchor points) isn't considered a bridging wall. Skin lines are already straight.

cura.bridge_wall_min_length.label: Minimum Bridge Wall Length
cura.bridge_wall_min_length.tooltip: Unsupported walls shorter than this will be printed using the normal wall settings. Longer unsupported walls will be printed using the bridge wall settings.

cura.bridge_skin_support_threshold.label: Bridge Skin Support Threshold
cura.bridge_skin_support_threshold.tooltip: If a skin region is supported for less than this percentage of its area, print it using the bridge settings. Otherwise it is printed using the normal skin settings.

cura.bridge_wall_coast.label: Bridge Wall Coasting
cura.bridge_wall_coast.tooltip: This controls the distance the extruder should coast immediately before a bridge wall begins. Coasting before the bridge starts can reduce the pressure in the nozzle and may produce a flatter bridge.

cura.bridge_wall_speed.label: Bridge Wall Speed
cura.bridge_wall_speed.tooltip: The speed at which the bridge walls are printed.

cura.bridge_wall_material_flow.label: Bridge Wall Flow
cura.bridge_wall_material_flow.tooltip: When printing bridge walls, the amount of material extruded is multiplied by this value.

cura.bridge_skin_speed.label: Bridge Skin Speed
cura.bridge_skin_speed.tooltip: The speed at which bridge skin regions are printed.

cura.bridge_skin_material_flow.label: Bridge Skin Flow
cura.bridge_skin_material_flow.tooltip: When printing bridge skin regions, the amount of material extruded is multiplied by this value.

cura.bridge_skin_density.label: Bridge Skin Density
cura.bridge_skin_density.tooltip: The density of the bridge skin layer. Values less than 100 will increase the gaps between the skin lines.

cura.bridge_fan_speed.label: Bridge Fan Speed
cura.bridge_fan_speed.tooltip: Percentage fan speed to use when printing bridge walls and skin.

cura.bridge_interlace_lines.label: Interlace Bridge Lines
cura.bridge_interlace_lines.tooltip: When enabled, bridging lines will be printed interlaced, i.e. in 2 monotonic passes so that adjacent lines won't be printed just after each other. The lines of the first pass then have more time to cool down and are stronger when the second pass is added.

cura.bridge_enable_more_layers.label: Bridge Has Multiple Layers
cura.bridge_enable_more_layers.tooltip: If enabled, the second and third layers above the air are printed using the following settings. Otherwise, those layers are printed using the normal settings.

cura.bridge_skin_speed_2.label: Bridge Second Skin Speed
cura.bridge_skin_speed_2.tooltip: Print speed to use when printing the second bridge skin layer.

cura.bridge_skin_material_flow_2.label: Bridge Second Skin Flow
cura.bridge_skin_material_flow_2.tooltip: When printing the second bridge skin layer, the amount of material extruded is multiplied by this value.

cura.bridge_skin_density_2.label: Bridge Second Skin Density
cura.bridge_skin_density_2.tooltip: The density of the second bridge skin layer. Values less than 100 will increase the gaps between the skin lines.

cura.bridge_fan_speed_2.label: Bridge Second Skin Fan Speed
cura.bridge_fan_speed_2.tooltip: Percentage fan speed to use when printing the second bridge skin layer.

cura.bridge_skin_speed_3.label: Bridge Third Skin Speed
cura.bridge_skin_speed_3.tooltip: Print speed to use when printing the third bridge skin layer.

cura.bridge_skin_material_flow_3.label: Bridge Third Skin Flow
cura.bridge_skin_material_flow_3.tooltip: When printing the third bridge skin layer, the amount of material extruded is multiplied by this value.

cura.bridge_skin_density_3.label: Bridge Third Skin Density
cura.bridge_skin_density_3.tooltip: The density of the third bridge skin layer. Values less than 100 will increase the gaps between the skin lines.

cura.bridge_fan_speed_3.label: Bridge Third Skin Fan Speed
cura.bridge_fan_speed_3.tooltip: Percentage fan speed to use when printing the third bridge skin layer.

cura.clean_between_layers.label: Wipe Nozzle Between Layers
cura.clean_between_layers.tooltip: Whether to include nozzle wipe G-Code between layers (maximum 1 per layer). Enabling this setting could influence behavior of retract at layer change. Please use Wipe Retraction settings to control retraction at layers where the wipe script will be working.

cura.max_extrusion_before_wipe.label: Material Volume Between Wipes
cura.max_extrusion_before_wipe.tooltip: Maximum material that can be extruded before another nozzle wipe is initiated. If this value is less than the volume of material required in a layer, the setting has no effect in this layer, i.e. it is limited to one wipe per layer.

cura.wipe_retraction_enable.label: Wipe Retraction Enable
cura.wipe_retraction_enable.tooltip: Retract the filament when the nozzle is moving over a non-printed area.

cura.wipe_retraction_amount.label: Wipe Retraction Distance
cura.wipe_retraction_amount.tooltip: Amount to retract the filament so it does not ooze during the wipe sequence.

cura.wipe_retraction_extra_prime_amount.label: Wipe Retraction Extra Prime Amount
cura.wipe_retraction_extra_prime_amount.tooltip: Some material can ooze away during a wipe travel moves, which can be compensated for here.

cura.wipe_retraction_speed.label: Wipe Retraction Speed
cura.wipe_retraction_speed.tooltip: The speed at which the filament is retracted and primed during a wipe retraction move.

cura.wipe_retraction_retract_speed.label: Wipe Retraction Retract Speed
cura.wipe_retraction_retract_speed.tooltip: The speed at which the filament is retracted during a wipe retraction move.

cura.wipe_retraction_prime_speed.label: Wipe Retraction Prime Speed
cura.wipe_retraction_prime_speed.tooltip: The speed at which the filament is primed during a wipe retraction move.

cura.wipe_hop_enable.label: Wipe Z Hop
cura.wipe_hop_enable.tooltip: When wiping, the build plate is lowered to create clearance between the nozzle and the print. It prevents the nozzle from hitting the print during travel moves, reducing the chance to knock the print from the build plate.

cura.wipe_hop_amount.label: Wipe Z Hop Height
cura.wipe_hop_amount.tooltip: The height difference when performing a Z Hop.

cura.wipe_hop_speed.label: Wipe Hop Speed
cura.wipe_hop_speed.tooltip: Speed to move the z-axis during the hop.

cura.wipe_brush_pos_x.label: Wipe Brush X Position
cura.wipe_brush_pos_x.tooltip: X location where wipe script will start.

cura.wipe_repeat_count.label: Wipe Repeat Count
cura.wipe_repeat_count.tooltip: Number of times to move the nozzle across the brush.

cura.wipe_move_distance.label: Wipe Move Distance
cura.wipe_move_distance.tooltip: The distance to move the head back and forth across the brush.

cura.small_hole_max_size.label: Small Hole Max Size
cura.small_hole_max_size.tooltip: Holes and part outlines with a diameter smaller than this will be printed using Small Feature Speed.

cura.small_feature_max_length.label: Small Feature Max Length
cura.small_feature_max_length.tooltip: Feature outlines that are shorter than this length will be printed using Small Feature Speed.

cura.small_feature_speed_factor.label: Small Feature Speed
cura.small_feature_speed_factor.tooltip: Small features will be printed at this percentage of their normal print speed. Slower printing can help with adhesion and accuracy.

cura.small_feature_speed_factor_0.label: Small Feature Initial Layer Speed
cura.small_feature_speed_factor_0.tooltip: Small features on the first layer will be printed at this percentage of their normal print speed. Slower printing can help with adhesion and accuracy.

cura.material_alternate_walls.label: Alternate Wall Directions
cura.material_alternate_walls.tooltip: Alternate wall directions every other layer and inset. Useful for materials that can build up stress, like for metal printing.

cura.group_outer_walls.label: Group Outer Walls
cura.group_outer_walls.tooltip: Outer walls of different islands in the same layer are printed in sequence. When enabled the amount of flow changes is limited because walls are printed one type at a time, when disabled the number of travels between islands is reduced because walls in the same islands are grouped.

cura.retraction_during_travel_ratio.label: Retraction During Travel Move
cura.retraction_during_travel_ratio.tooltip:
The ratio of retraction performed during the travel move, with the remainder completed while the nozzle is stationary, before traveling
  • When 0, the entire retraction is performed while stationary, before the travel begins
  • When 100, the entire retraction is performed during the travel move, bypassing the stationary phase

cura.keep_retracting_during_travel.label: Keep Retracting During Travel
cura.keep_retracting_during_travel.tooltip: When retraction during travel is enabled, and there is more than enough time to perform a full retract during a travel move, spread the retraction over the whole travel move with a lower retraction speed, so that we do not travel with a non-retracting nozzle. This can help reducing oozing.

cura.prime_during_travel_ratio.label: Prime During Travel Move
cura.prime_during_travel_ratio.tooltip:
The ratio of priming performed during the travel move, with the remainder completed while the nozzle is stationary, after traveling
  • When 0, the entire priming is performed while stationary, after the travel ends
  • When 100, the entire priming is performed during the travel move, allowing the print to start immediately

cura.scarf_joint_seam_length.label: Scarf Seam Length
cura.scarf_joint_seam_length.tooltip: Determines the length of the scarf seam, a seam type that should make the Z seam less visible. Must be higher than 0 to be effective.

cura.scarf_joint_seam_start_height_ratio.label: Scarf Seam Start Height
cura.scarf_joint_seam_start_height_ratio.tooltip: The ratio of the selected layer height at which the scarf seam will begin. A lower number will result in a larger seam height. Must be lower than 100 to be effective.

cura.scarf_split_distance.label: Scarf Seam Step Length
cura.scarf_split_distance.tooltip: Determines the length of each step in the flow change when extruding along the scarf seam. A smaller distance will result in a more precise but also more complex G-code.

cura.wall_0_start_speed_ratio.label: Outer Wall Start Speed Ratio
cura.wall_0_start_speed_ratio.tooltip: This is the ratio of the top speed to start with when printing an outer wall.

cura.wall_0_acceleration.label: Outer Wall Start Acceleration
cura.wall_0_acceleration.tooltip: This is the acceleration with which to reach the top speed when printing an outer wall.

cura.wall_0_end_speed_ratio.label: Outer Wall End Speed Ratio
cura.wall_0_end_speed_ratio.tooltip: This is the ratio of the top speed to end with when printing an outer wall.

cura.wall_0_deceleration.label: Outer Wall End Deceleration
cura.wall_0_deceleration.tooltip: This is the deceleration with which to end printing an outer wall.

cura.wall_0_speed_split_distance.label: Outer Wall Speed Split Distance
cura.wall_0_speed_split_distance.tooltip: This is the maximum length of an extrusion path when splitting a longer path to apply the outer wall acceleration/deceleration. A smaller distance will create a more precise but also more verbose G-Code.

cura.minimum_infill_line_length.label: Minimum Infill Line Length
cura.minimum_infill_line_length.tooltip: When an infill area generates lines with a total length lower than this value, they will be discarded to avoid printing lots of tiny useless lines. It can help reduce travel moves, retractions and unretractions.

cura.material_delta_temperature_roofing.label: Temperature Delta Top Surface
cura.material_delta_temperature_roofing.tooltip: A temperature delta to be applied when printing the top-surface layers. This can help with getting a smoother surface when printing at very high speed. Note that it will be applied without waiting for the temperature to be reached, so it should remain low.

cura.ppr_enable.label: Enable Print Process Reporting
cura.ppr_enable.tooltip: Enable print process reporting for setting threshold values for possible fault detection.

cura.flow_warn_limit.label: Flow Warning
cura.flow_warn_limit.tooltip: Limit on the flow warning for detection.

cura.flow_anomaly_limit.label: Flow Limit
cura.flow_anomaly_limit.tooltip: Limit on flow anomaly for detection.

cura.print_temp_warn_limit.label: Print temperature Warning
cura.print_temp_warn_limit.tooltip: Limit on Print temperature warning for detection.

cura.print_temp_anomaly_limit.label: Print temperature Limit
cura.print_temp_anomaly_limit.tooltip: Limit on Print Temperature anomaly for detection.

cura.bv_temp_warn_limit.label: Build Volume temperature Warning
cura.bv_temp_warn_limit.tooltip: Limit on Build Volume Temperature warning for detection.

cura.bv_temp_anomaly_limit.label: Build Volume temperature Limit
cura.bv_temp_anomaly_limit.tooltip: Limit on Build Volume temperature Anomaly for detection.

cura.center_object.label: Center Object
cura.center_object.tooltip: Whether to center the object on the middle of the build platform (0,0), instead of using the coordinate system in which the object was saved.

cura.mesh_position_x.label: Mesh Position X
cura.mesh_position_x.tooltip: Offset applied to the object in the x direction.

cura.mesh_position_y.label: Mesh Position Y
cura.mesh_position_y.tooltip: Offset applied to the object in the y direction.

cura.mesh_position_z.label: Mesh Position Z
cura.mesh_position_z.tooltip: Offset applied to the object in the z direction. With this you can perform what was used to be called 'Object Sink'.

cura.mesh_rotation_matrix.label: Mesh Rotation Matrix
cura.mesh_rotation_matrix.tooltip: Transformation matrix to be applied to the model when loading it from file.

cura.material_id.label: Cura Material ID
cura.material_id.tooltip: The ID of the material that is used internally.

cura.material_name.label: Material Name
cura.material_name.tooltip: The fully qualified material name, e.g. 'UltiMaker PLA White'.

cura.material_spool_cost.label: Material Spool Cost
cura.material_spool_cost.tooltip: The cost of a full spool of material.

cura.material_spool_weight.label: Material Spool Weight
cura.material_spool_weight.tooltip: The weight of a full spool of material, in grams.

cura.extruder_nr.label: Extruder
cura.extruder_nr.tooltip: The extruder train used for printing. This is used in multi-extrusion.

cura.machine_extruder_change_duration.label: Extruder Change duration
cura.machine_extruder_change_duration.tooltip: When using a multi tool setup, this value is the tool change time in seconds.  This value will be added to the estimate time based on the number of changes that occur.

cura.machine_extruder_cooling_fan_number.label: Extruder Print Cooling Fan
cura.machine_extruder_cooling_fan_number.tooltip: The number of the print cooling fan associated with this extruder. Only change this from the default value of 0 when you have a different print cooling fan for each extruder.

cura.machine_extruder_end_code.label: Extruder End G-Code
cura.machine_extruder_end_code.tooltip: End g-code to execute when switching away from this extruder.

cura.machine_extruder_end_code_duration.label: Extruder End G-Code Duration
cura.machine_extruder_end_code_duration.tooltip: The time it takes to execute the end g-code, when switching away from this extruder.

cura.machine_extruder_end_pos_abs.label: Extruder End Position Absolute
cura.machine_extruder_end_pos_abs.tooltip: Make the extruder ending position absolute rather than relative to the last-known location of the head.

cura.machine_extruder_end_pos_x.label: Extruder End Position X
cura.machine_extruder_end_pos_x.tooltip: The x-coordinate of the ending position when turning the extruder off.

cura.machine_extruder_end_pos_y.label: Extruder End Position Y
cura.machine_extruder_end_pos_y.tooltip: The y-coordinate of the ending position when turning the extruder off.

cura.machine_extruder_prestart_code.label: Extruder Prestart G-Code
cura.machine_extruder_prestart_code.tooltip: Prestart g-code to execute before switching to this extruder.

cura.machine_extruder_start_code_duratio.label: Extruder Start G-Code Duration
cura.machine_extruder_start_code_duratio.tooltip: The time it'll take to execute the start g-code, when switching to this extruder.

cura.machine_extruder_start_pos_abs.label: Extruder Start Position Absolute
cura.machine_extruder_start_pos_abs.tooltip: Make the extruder starting position absolute rather than relative to the last-known location of the head.

cura.machine_extruder_start_pos_x.label: Extruder Start Position X
cura.machine_extruder_start_pos_x.tooltip: The x-coordinate of the starting position when turning the extruder on.

cura.machine_extruder_start_pos_y.label: Extruder Start Position Y
cura.machine_extruder_start_pos_y.tooltip: The y-coordinate of the starting position when turning the extruder on.

cura.machine_nozzle_head_distance.label: Nozzle Length
cura.machine_nozzle_head_distance.tooltip: The height difference between the tip of the nozzle and the lowest part of the print head.
